docs.title: Best three for Group B
docs.text:
1. ScanNet++ iPhone part. Only set with raw ARKit poses and iPhone LiDAR depth registered to sub-millimetre laser scans on 1,000+ rooms. Apply early because approval is by hand; confirm licence fit first, since commercial use is prohibited.
  2. LaMAR. The only verified source of both iPhone ARKit and Android ARCore device poses, with laser-scan alignment. It tests the Android capture-app pose pipeline and metric alignment outdoors as well as in. Access is by form and sizes are unknown.
  3. MuSHRoom (iPhone part) for a small laser-referenced set, with ADVIO for ARKit versus ARCore drift. MuSHRoom is one 36 GB download of ten rooms with a Faro mesh, but its licence is stated three different ways. ADVIO is 5 GB, parallel iPhone and Pixel tracks, CC BY-NC. Use ADVIO if only an Android versus iOS comparison is needed.

docs.title: Mapping to Recce needs
docs.text:
• Drone GPS as pose prior (RC-P8 style): EuroSDR RPAS phases 1 and 2 compare no-RTK and RTK priors against surveyed checkpoints. Mill 19 and GauU-Scene supply drone-log positions but no independent reference.
  • Metric scale and frame checks: EuroSDR RPAS (GCP and checkpoint coordinates, TLS), ScanNet++ and MuSHRoom (laser meshes), MobileBrick (exact brick geometry).
  • 1,000+ image distribution: EuroSDR P1 flight (about 1,000), Mill 19 (1,940 and 1,678), GauU-Scene scenes (up to 1,215), UrbanScene3D and SkyLume (far larger and non-commercial).
  • Android device poses: LaMAR (ARCore), ADVIO (Pixel ARCore), Map-free (ARCore or ARKit, undistinguished), Objectron (ARCore or ARKit, undistinguished).
  • Licence flag for everything above: only EuroSDR RPAS (CC BY 4.0) and GauU-Scene (CC BY 4.0 in the paper) are clearly permissive. Non-commercial or restricted: UseGeo, ScanNet++, UrbanScene3D, SkyLume (per paper), Map-free, ADVIO, egenioussBench. Unclear: MuSHRoom, H3D, UAVD4L, WildUAV, LaMAR data, Mill 19 data.

docs.title: Could not verify
docs.text:
• EuroSDR RPAS: which phase archives hold which flights; exact camera EXIF content (GPS tags) in the images; whether the quarry TLS cloud and the checkpoints sit in Phase 1, 2 or 3 files (the paper says data came in phases; the Zenodo page lists only archive sizes).
  • UseGeo: GNSS per image, GCP use, LiDAR sensor accuracy, download sizes, and whether the GitHub README holds licence text beyond the one statement relayed by the page fetch. The FBK dataset page and the paper PDF returned no detail (the paper PDF returned HTTP 403).
  • H3D: licence, download sizes, and whether original images (not only point cloud and mesh) are released.
  • Dortmund and Toronto/Vaihingen oblique benchmark sets named in the task: the IFP benchmark page lists Zurich oblique, Vaihingen/Enz and Munchen; Dortmund and Toronto did not appear in the fetched text, and no download size was shown.
  • Mill 19: GPS/IMU presence in the released archives, dataset licence (only the repository MIT licence seen), archive sizes.
  • UrbanScene3D: per-image GPS or poses for the real scenes, image count of the real scenes, whether a single scene can be fetched.
  • GauU-Scene V2: working download URL (the paper hides it for review) and per-scene sizes.
  • SkyLume: real licence (paper says CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, project page says none) and whether one region can be fetched without the 1.5 TB preview.
  • WildUAV: licence terms in WildUAV_License.pdf and image counts.
  • UAVD4L: image counts, licence, file sizes (Baidu hosting only).
  • SensatUrban: licence and size (not checked after finding it contains no images).
  • ScanNet++: whether single scenes can be downloaded alone; per-scene size; the claim that iPhone poses are raw ARKit output comes from the documentation page ("ARKit poses") but the v2 poses may have been refined (the news item mentions updated poses, not read in detail).
  • MuSHRoom: which of the three licence statements governs the data; whether any raw ARKit (not Polycam) poses ship.
  • LaMAR: data licence and per-scene sizes (behind the access form); counts of ARKit versus ARCore sessions.
  • Map-free: whether any session is Android or the poses are all ARKit; download size.
  • ADVIO: image frame count and resolution (not read).
  • Objectron: counts of Android versus iOS clips.
  • MobileBrick: device model, pose source and download size.
  • egenioussBench: download size and the smartphone model.
  • Stray Scanner: public datasets recorded with it. None found, so none are listed.
  • Google ARCore-specific dataset beyond Objectron and LaMAR, and any Android phone-with-ToF-plus-TLS dataset: searched, none found; the searches may have missed one.

docs.title: Research: the photogrammetry landscape (2026-11-23)
docs.text:
Corrections (2026-11-23, from the tools overview pass): KHR_gaussian_splatting is ratified, not a release candidate — the spec README on Khronos main reads "Complete, Ratified by the Khronos Group". LightGlue's README states its weights are Apache-2.0; only SuperPoint and its weights are restrictive, so "LightGlue weights inherit SuperPoint's restriction" below is wrong. Current figures live in tools overview.

Input to the brief and the prototype plan. Gathered by a research agent from web sources on 2026-11-23. [V] means confirmed on a primary page that day, with the URL. [U] means from memory or a search snippet only, not checked. Treat every [U] as a lead, not a fact.

docs.title: Open-source pipelines
docs.text:
• COLMAP [V] — BSD-3. GLOMAP (global SfM) is merged in. CUDA wheels on PyPI; AMD via HIP/ROCm builds. The format hub: nearly every other tool imports or exports COLMAP. https://github.com/colmap/colmap
  • WebODM [V, partly] — AGPL-3.0. Django 5.2 + Celery + PostgreSQL + Valkey, processing on NodeODM workers (engine now named "ODX"). Outputs orthophotos, point clouds, DEMs, textured meshes, and now gaussian splats. NodeODM has its own small REST API (task new / upload / status / output / cancel) [U]; one WebODM schedules onto many nodes [U]. The closest analogue to "web UI + API + workers", but aerial-only: no object, fisheye, RAW or known-pose workflow. https://github.com/WebODM/WebODM
  • gsplat [V] — Apache-2.0. Pinhole and fisheye, 3DGUT, MCMC. No prebuilt aarch64 wheels; JIT build. https://github.com/nerfstudio-project/gsplat
  • Brush [V] — Apache-2.0. Splat training on wgpu (no CUDA): Mac, Windows, Linux, Android, web. Trains from COLMAP or nerfstudio data; supports masks. https://github.com/ArthurBrussee/brush
  • nerfstudio [U] — Apache-2.0; ran at 1.1.5 on a GB10 in one write-up.
  • OpenMVG (MPL2), OpenMVS (AGPL3 — a risk for a hosted service), AliceVision/Meshroom (MPL2), OpenSplat (AGPL3), Instant-NGP (NVIDIA non-commercial), 2DGS / PGSR (research code, licences unchecked) [all U].

docs.title: Learned feed-forward SfM
docs.text:
Model Code Weights Notes VGGT (Meta/Oxford) not captured [U] VGGT-1B non-commercial; VGGT-1B-Commercial gated by form [V] CVPR 2025 best paper; COLMAP export; "VGGT-Omega" May 2026, licence unread. https://github.com/facebookresearch/vggt MapAnything (Meta) Apache-2.0 [V] map-anything CC-BY-NC; map-anything-apache Apache-2.0 [V] Takes optional intrinsics, poses, depth; metric output; up to ~2,000 views on 140 GB. https://github.com/facebookresearch/map-anything Pi3 / Pi3X BSD-3 [V] CC-BY-NC 4.0 [V] Pi3X accepts optional pose/intrinsics/depth; approximate metric scale. https://github.com/yyfz/Pi3 DUSt3R / MASt3R / MASt3R-SfM (Naver) CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 [V] same [V] Non-commercial. https://github.com/naver/mast3r

Feed-forward models run at low resolution (~518 px for VGGT [U]). Use them for initialisation, pose priors, metric scale and sparse-view cases; COLMAP/GLOMAP bundle adjustment stays the accuracy engine. No head-to-head numbers were checked.

docs.title: Feature matching [all U]
docs.text: SuperPoint weights: restrictive (Magic Leap); LightGlue weights trained on SuperPoint inherit it. ALIKED BSD-3, RoMa MIT, hloc Apache-2.0. A clean stack: ALIKED+LightGlue or RoMa, weights checked.

docs.title: Commercial tools
docs.text:
• RealityScan (Epic, ex-RealityCapture) [V via news]: free under $1M revenue, $1,250/seat/year above. 2.1 (Nov 2025) added CLI importColmap and a Remote Command plugin (REST/gRPC); 2.2 (Jun 2026) added AMD GPUs. Windows-only [U].
  • Agisoft Metashape [partly V]: Python API, scripting in Professional only. A metashape-mcp package exists on PyPI (106 tools reported; author and licence unverified).
  • Polycam (API mentioned), KIRI Engine (pay-per-credit API incl. 3DGS-to-mesh) [V]; Luma ($1/capture API, possibly stale), Pix4D, Scaniverse, Apple Object Capture (macOS/iOS only, USDZ out) [U].

docs.title: MCP and agents
docs.text: metashape-mcp (above) and the paper "SceneAgent" (arXiv 2610.34745, unread). Two searches found no MCP server for COLMAP or splat training — a fact about two searches, not proof of a gap.

docs.title: Formats and viewers
docs.text:
• KHR_gaussian_splatting reached release candidate 2026-02-04, with KHR_gaussian_splatting_compression_spz [V]. https://digitalproduction.com/2026/02/04/gltf-learns-to-splat-without-losing-the-plot/
  • PlayCanvas reads PLY, SOG, SPZ and splat-GLB; splat-transform converts between them [V].
  • Cesium 3D Tiles added LOD splats in April 2026 [V].
  • GLB for web meshes, USDZ for Apple/AR, PLY/OBJ for interchange; three.js, Babylon, SuperSplat, Spark, potree as viewers [U].

docs.title: ARM64 / GB10
docs.text: One blog (not NVIDIA) ran COLMAP, gsplat and nerfstudio on a GB10: DGX OS on Ubuntu 24.04, CUDA 13.0, compute capability 12.1, PyTorch 2.9.0+cu130. It needed TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=12.0, and apt COLMAP fell back to CPU SIFT headless. https://dev.classmethod.jp/en/articles/dgx-spark-3dgs-digital-twin/

docs.title: Gaps the research agent named (its judgement, unsourced)
docs.text:
1. Agent-readable quality state: coverage, reprojection error, unregistered images, "capture more here".
  2. Hybrid: feed-forward poses and scale, verified by COLMAP bundle adjustment, with fallback.
  3. Robot-supplied poses and intrinsics as first-class input.
  4. Mixed sensors in one scene (iPhone LiDAR, GoPro fisheye, DSLR RAW).
  5. Production-quality textured mesh from splats.
  6. A licence-clean, commercial-safe stack.
  7. Tested ARM64 containers for the whole stack.

docs.title: Not verified
docs.text: Pix4D, Scaniverse, Object Capture details; OpenMVS, AliceVision, OpenSplat, Instant-NGP status; DUSt3R, VGGT-Omega and SAM 3 licences; web viewer status; Luma pricing; metashape-mcp provenance; most release dates.

docs.title: Research: Metashape, other tools, underwater, cameras (2026-11-23)
docs.text: Second research pass, by a research agent on 2026-11-23. [V] = read on a primary page that day (URL given). [U] = memory, search snippet or not confirmed. The Metashape manual cited is the 2.3 Professional PDF (https://www.agisoft.com/pdf/metashape-pro_2_3_en.pdf).

docs.title: Agisoft Metashape — the industry reference
docs.text:
• Editions: Standard $179, Professional $3,499, both perpetual node-locked [V https://www.agisoft.com/buy/online-store/]. Professional adds Python scripting, network and cloud processing, 4D, DEM and orthomosaic [V compare page + manual]. Version 2.3.x [V]; release date unclear [U].
  • Workflow [V manual]:
  • Align photos: accuracy Highest (4× upscale) … Lowest (1/16 px); preselection Generic / Reference / Estimated / Sequential; tie point limit (10,000 recommended); guided matching; adaptive camera model fitting; exclude stationary tie points (turntable without masks); masks applied to key or tie points.
  • Clean tie points by reprojection error, reconstruction uncertainty, image count, projection accuracy; Optimize Cameras re-runs bundle adjustment.
  • Depth maps (quality Ultra High down; filtering Mild / Moderate / Aggressive / Disabled) → point cloud → mesh (face count, interpolation) → texture (diffuse, occlusion, normal; Mosaic / Average / NaturalBlending in 2.3).
  • DEM and orthomosaic (geographic, planar, cylindrical projections; seamline editing; GeoTIFF).
  • Camera models: frame, fisheye, spherical, cylindrical, RPC; 2.3 adds equidistant and equisolid fisheye. The manual advises avoiding fisheye and ultra-wide lenses.
  • iPhone/iPad TrueDepth images load with depth; rear LiDAR not mentioned.
  • 2.2: COLMAP export, AI masks, AprilTag [U]. 2.3: NaturalBlending, texture editing, automatic colour enhancement, LiDAR and GNSS bias tools [V]. No gaussian splats in 2.3 notes [V].
  • Network processing [V manual]: a server holding the task queue (does no processing, not fault tolerant), workers computing onto shared storage at the same absolute path, clients plus a Network Monitor. Work is split per task (batch step); 2.3 adds concurrent independent tasks. Task-level parallelism, not one alignment spread across nodes (finer splitting unverified).
  • GPU [V manual]: CUDA and OpenCL 1.2; Vulkan for texture blending. Metal not mentioned.
  • Sentiment [U, aggregator snippets]: praised for accuracy, maturity, Python API; criticised for Professional's price, node-locking, slowness on large jobs.

docs.title: Other tools, one line each
docs.text:
• 3DF Zephyr — free tier (50 photos), Lite €199, Pro €4,200 or €250/month; photogrammetry plus laser scans with GIS/CAD tools [V https://www.3dflow.net/3df-zephyr-photogrammetry-software/].
  • Pix4Dmatic — large-scale, survey and CAD vectors, linked to PIX4Dcatch mobile capture and PIX4Dcloud [V https://www.pix4d.com/product/pix4dmatic/].
  • DJI Terra — photogrammetry, 3D gaussian splatting, multispectral, LiDAR, cluster reconstruction; DJI-tied; trial capped at 500 photos [V https://enterprise.dji.com/dji-terra].
  • Meshroom — MPL-2.0 node graph with caching, local or render farm, plugins for depth and splatting [V https://github.com/alicevision/Meshroom].
  • RealityScan, iTwin Capture — features not verified [U].

docs.title: Underwater
docs.text:
• Refraction: flat ports cause depth-dependent systematic error; dome ports mostly remove it only when the lens entrance pupil sits at the dome centre. Brown models absorb refraction only implicitly; radial weighting improved flat-port accuracy up to 50% [V https://isprs-archives.copernicus.org/articles/XLIII-B2-2020/977/2020/]. Commercial tools reportedly have no explicit refraction model [U].
  • Refractive COLMAP (IROS 2024) supports flat and dome ports; open source; licence not stated [V https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.08640].
  • Colour: Sea-thru (Akkaynak & Treibitz, CVPR 2019) needs per-pixel range; no official code. Teragion/Sea-Thru-Impl is GPL-3.0/MIT, small [V https://github.com/Teragion/Sea-Thru-Impl]. A reconstruction supplies the range Sea-thru needs — so colour correction after geometry, with an uncorrected copy kept for features, is a natural fit (agent's reasoning, unsourced).
  • Splats/NeRF underwater: WaterSplatting Apache-2.0 (nerfstudio 1.1.4, CUDA 11.8) [V https://github.com/water-splatting/water-splatting]; SeaThru-NeRF Apache-2.0 [V https://github.com/deborahLevy130/seathru_NeRF]; RUSplatting research-only [V]; SeaSplat licence unknown [U].
  • Reef monitoring: 100 Island Challenge uses Viscore for viewing large SfM models [V https://chei.ucsd.edu/?p=2805]. TagLab is GPL-3.0 AI-assisted segmentation and annotation with SAM [V https://github.com/cnr-isti-vclab/TagLab]. Which reconstruction software reef groups use was not established.
  • Not covered: backscatter, caustics, moving subjects, scale methods (bars, lasers, stereo), swim patterns and image counts.

docs.title: Cameras
docs.text:
• RAW: LibRaw 0.22 lists the D850 and the Sony ILCE-1 (A1) [V https://www.libraw.org/supported-cameras]; compressed ARW not stated. rawpy is MIT with LGPL LibRaw [V https://github.com/letmaik/rawpy]; its bundled LibRaw version unchecked.
  • GoPro GPMF: accelerometer (~200 Hz), gyro, GPS, magnetometer, shutter, ISO, orientation quaternions, gravity; HERO5–HERO13 and MAX; parser Apache-2.0/MIT [V https://github.com/gopro/gpmf-parser]. No evidence found of GPMF used as an SfM prior.
  • iPhone: Record3D streams RGB-D with LiDAR, camera poses and confidence maps over USB; library LGPL-2.1 [V https://github.com/marek-simonik/record3d]. ProRAW, HEIC depth, Polycam / Scaniverse / NeRFCapture exports not verified.
  • DJI Mini 4 Pro: MSDK v5 supports it only with the RC-N2 controller, not the RC 2 [V https://dronedj.com/2025/03/21/dji-mini-4-pro-msdk/]; Litchi, Maven, Drone Harmony named. EXIF/XMP fields unverified.

docs.title: Feature set (agent's synthesis — design judgement, not sourced)
docs.text:
Table stakes: JPEG + NEF/ARW ingest; EXIF focal, GPS and gimbal priors; COLMAP-class SfM with preselection; dense mesh + point cloud + texture, exported PLY/OBJ/glTF; scale (markers or scale bars) and coordinate transform; masks incl. automatic background; a distributed job queue with per-task status; HTTP API and MCP over the same job model.

Differentiators: refraction-aware camera option (flat/dome port); depth-aware colour correction after reconstruction; gaussian splats from the same poses (Metashape 2.3 has none); GoPro GPMF and ARKit/Record3D priors; per-machine backends incl. Apple silicon (Metashape documents no Metal); drone missions later (Mini 4 Pro needs the RC-N2).

docs.title: Not verified
docs.text: Metashape education prices, full edition table, marker/target and chunk details, 2.3 release date, real forum sentiment; RealityScan and iTwin features; reef groups' software, NOAA workflow, Sandin Lab SOP, CoralNet; backscatter/caustics/scale research; GoPro lens modes; iPhone ProRAW and capture app exports; Mini 4 Pro XMP; Refractive COLMAP and SeaSplat licences; A1 compressed ARW in rawpy.

docs.title: UX inspiration research for the scene and the explanations
docs.text:
Date: 2026-11-24. Method: web search and page fetches run on 2026-11-24, outside photogrammetry software on purpose, harvesting interaction concepts from current products and explanatory work. Every fetched page was summarised by a small model before it reached the author, so a [V] claim is accurate to that summary and not to the page's exact wording; a claim that needs exact wording needs a second read before it enters a UX spec. Frame and scene follow the "Two registers in one interface" paragraph of the brief §2 and the eight ideas in visual ideas.

Legend:

  • [V] read on a primary page today; the URL follows the claim. Vendor documentation, vendor blogs and the author's own site count as primary. Trade press that reports on a vendor is marked "(trade press)".
  • [U] from memory, from a search-result snippet, or from a page that failed to load. Unconfirmed; treat as a lead, not a fact. A snippet URL is given where one exists.

Idea numbers #1 to #8 refer to the table in visual ideas. "NEW" refers to the list in the section "New ideas" below.

docs.title: 1. Autodesk and the generative 3D wave
docs.text:
Flow Studio 3D Editor and Canvas. Flow Studio splits generative work into two surfaces. The Canvas is a node-based 2D workspace for image and video generation and refinement; the 3D Editor is a spatial surface where characters, environments, camera tracks and motion capture are assembled "before generation occurs", with blocking, composition and camera movement set by hand rather than by prompt. [V] https://digitalproduction.com/2026/08/04/autodesk-flow-studio-adds-3d-editor-and-canvas/ (trade press). The pattern: direct the scene spatially first, then let the model render it. The delight is control without a text box; the person points, the machine fills in.

Recce mapping: the same inversion applies to capture planning. A ghost camera (#3) is placed in 3D by hand or by an agent, and the engine then judges the plan. The Canvas-versus-3D-Editor split also maps to Recce's two registers: a node-like run view in the frame, the spatial scene in the viewport.

Neural Layer and AI Rigging. AI Rigging places skeletal joints on a generated character "in a few clicks" and previews the rig in the app before export to Maya, Blender or Unreal; Neural Layer refines materials and lighting inside a Live Action project without a traditional render pipeline, priced at 15 credits per second of footage. [V] https://blogs.autodesk.com/media-and-entertainment/2026/04/28/introducing-ai-rigging-and-neural-layer-in-autodesk-flow-studio/ . The pattern that transfers is the visible cost per unit of output: the price is stated next to the action. Recce runs on the owner's hardware, so the equivalent is a stated time and energy estimate on a recipe before it runs.

Wonder 3D, text and image to 3D. Flow Studio adds a generative model for text to 3D and image to 3D, available at all subscription levels. [U] search snippet, https://adsknews.autodesk.com/en/news/autodesk-flow-studio-launches-wonder-3d-gen-ai-model-to-help-creators-make-3d-characters-and-objects-faster-and-easier/ . Relevance to Recce is indirect: a generated model has no coverage or uncertainty, a reconstruction has both, and that is the product difference to make visible.

Neural CAD and Project Bernini. Autodesk describes foundation models trained on CAD data, shown first as Project Bernini in May 2024, aimed at Fusion and Forma, where "you will watch the neural CAD engine reason through your request". [U] search snippet, https://www.autodesk.com/design-make/articles/neural-cad (the page returned HTTP 403 to the fetch). The claim to test later is the UX phrase "watch it reason": the reasoning is shown as an event stream the person can follow, which is the shape of idea #5.

Forma analysis layers. Forma runs sun, wind, noise, microclimate and embodied-carbon analyses on a massing model and re-evaluates within seconds of an edit, using ML predictors for the rapid versions. [U] search snippet, https://illustrarch.com/articles/design-softwares/73363-autodesk-forma-review.html (the vendor page returned HTTP 403). The concept is an analysis painted onto the model that updates live while the person moves geometry. In Recce the analysis is coverage and uncertainty; the live-edit equivalent is dragging a ghost camera and watching the surrounding surface relight (#3, #4) from a cheap predictor, with the exact recomputation following later.

Maya, 3ds Max, Fusion recent UX. A search returned a trade-press headline that Autodesk released major updates across Maya, 3ds Max, Flow Studio and Arnold. [U] https://awn.com/print/news/autodesk-releases-major-updates-across-maya-3ds-max-flow-studio-and-arnold . The article was not read. The Autodesk University 2026 announcements page returned HTTP 403, so no AU 2026 claim is made here.

docs.title: 2. Creative 3D tools winning new users
docs.text:
Blender 5.0 (released 2025-11-18). The release notes list: "Full Screen Area" renamed "Focus Mode"; more than 300 theme settings removed and the rest unified, including a shared playhead appearance across editors; group nodes show a stack indicator and open on double-click, with clickable breadcrumbs to navigate back out; a Swap Node operator (Shift+S) replaces a node type and keeps its connections; a "Reduce Motion" option; tree views gain multi-select, F2 rename and name search; animation editors share unified footer playback controls. [V] https://developer.blender.org/docs/release_notes/5.0/user_interface/ and https://developer.blender.org/docs/release_notes/5.0/ . Three transferable patterns: breadcrumbed drill-in for nested structure (a run contains stages, a stage contains steps), swap-in-place for a strategy that keeps its connections (COLMAP to GLOMAP with the inputs and outputs preserved, matching #6), and a Reduce Motion switch that Recce needs because idea #1 is animation-heavy.

Spline. A browser 3D tool with real-time multi-user editing, states and events for interaction, and publishing the same scene to web, iOS (SwiftUI) and Android. It exposes an MCP server so Claude, ChatGPT or Cursor agents can read the scene, write changes and frame views, and the person keeps editing the same file without a re-import. [V] https://spline.design/ . This is the closest existing example of Recce's agent face working on the visible scene: the agent edits what the person sees, in place. Mapping: an agent debrief (#5) that moves the camera to frame its evidence and drops annotations into the scene the person can then move or delete.

Womp. Browser modelling built on SDF/CSG "Liquid 3D" shapes that blend and merge, with iridescent and holographic material finishes, and an ordering path to physical prints. [V] https://womp.com/ . The concept is soft blending as the default response to input: shapes melt together instead of intersecting with hard edges. For Recce this suggests uncertainty drawn as a soft field that merges between neighbouring cameras (#4) rather than a patchwork of per-point colours.

Plasticity. Direct editing with no history tree, curvature-continuous fillets and surface blends. [V] https://www.plasticity.xyz/ . The recorded concept is direct manipulation with immediate geometric feedback. The feel (not the CAD content) is the reference for dragging a ghost camera.

Shapr3D. One interface across Windows, Mac, iPad, iPhone and Apple Vision Pro, Apple Pencil and SpaceMouse input, review links that open in a browser, and a claim that most users build a first model within 15 minutes. [V] https://www.shapr3d.com/ . The pattern is the browser review link: a reviewer needs no install. Recce's web UI is that by construction, so a shareable read-only link to a presentation scene (#7) is the matching feature.

Nomad Sculpt. The fetched page covered licensing only (activation per computer, a 15-day offline grace). [V] https://nomadsculpt.com/ . No UX claim about its gesture model is made from a read page. [U] From memory, Nomad's strength is a dense tool set made usable on a phone by large touch targets and a bottom tool shelf; unconfirmed.

Houdini. SideFX describes every action as a node, with nodes wired into networks that "define a 'recipe' that can be tweaked to explore different creative paths". [V] https://www.sidefx.com/products/houdini/ . The word is the same one Recce uses. Mapping: a Recce recipe is a node network whose comparison view (#6) highlights which node's parameter differs, rather than diffing two flat settings lists. [U] From memory, Houdini's geometry spreadsheet shows per-point attributes at any node and the viewport shows the network's state at the selected node; if confirmed, it is the model for "inspect the reconstruction as it stood after this stage".

Godot 4.5. Adds screen-reader support through AccessKit for the Project Manager, standard UI nodes and the inspector, translation preview in the editor viewport, colour swatches beside colour values in scripts, multi-node selection while debugging a running game, and editor language switching without restart. [V] https://godotengine.org/releases/4.5/ . The transferable idea is inline preview of a value where it is written: a swatch next to a colour. In Recce, a number in the inspector (overlap 0.7, focal length 24 mm) carries a small drawing beside it.

Cinema 4D 2027. Scatter (surface population), Liquid FX (foam, spray, bubbles) and Redshift speedups, plus viewport, node-editing and scene-management refinements. [V] https://www.maxon.net/en/cinema-4d . No UX concept beyond feature names was extracted. Unreal Engine 5.7 release notes returned HTTP 403, so nothing is claimed about the UE editor.

docs.title: 3. Colour, finishing and media
docs.text:
DaVinci Resolve 21. One application divided into page-sized workspaces (Photo, Cut, Edit, Color, Fusion, Fairlight, Deliver) switched with one click, with camera-original quality throughout; the Color page offers HDR colour wheels, curves, a node graph and Power Windows. [V] https://www.blackmagicdesign.com/products/davinciresolve . The concept is task pages: the same project, a different room per job. Recce's equivalent is a small set of rooms (Capture review, Registration, Coverage, Compare, Present, Debrief) over one run, each with its own tool set. [U] From memory, Resolve's still-store split-screen wipe compares a graded frame with a reference; it is the interaction behind #6.

Final Cut Pro. A magnetic timeline that keeps clips in sync while the editor experiments; Magnetic Mask separating people and objects without a green screen; Object Tracker; Visual Search and Transcript Search that find footage by what is in it or said in it. [V] https://www.apple.com/final-cut-pro/ . Two transfers: search by content (find "the photos that see the left hull" through the scene, not through file names) and tracking that attaches an annotation to a moving subject.

Capture One. Tethering with live view and focus assistance, custom workspaces and shortcuts, assisted masking, style matching. [V] https://www.captureone.com/en/features . Tethering is the pattern: a result appears on a large screen the moment the shutter fires. For Recce, a live capture session (a phone or a robot streaming photos) shows each frame registering into the model within seconds.

Lightroom. Release notes mention Assisted Culling with a Faces panel showing eye-sharpness and eyes-open scores per face, Adaptive Profiles, and a Color Variance slider. [U] search snippet, https://helpx.adobe.com/dk/lightroom/desktop/introduction/release-notes.html . The idea to keep is culling with a per-item score shown next to the thumbnail: each input photo carries a blur score, an overlap score and a "holds up N matches" count.

Halide. Mark III lists a 14-bit RAW waveform, colour zebras, focus peaking, a focus loupe and histograms, with a minimal-processing mode (Process Zero). [U] search snippet, https://lux.camera/halide-mark-iii/ (the vendor page returned HTTP 404 at a guessed path). The pattern is the measurement overlay: the image stays whole and the analysis lies over it as zebras and peaking, toggled by one control. Recce's coverage and confidence layers (#3, #4) take this form: overlays on the scene, one toggle each, never a separate chart.

Darkroom. Not fetched. [U] No claim is made.

docs.title: 4. iPhone and iPad capture apps
docs.text:
Apple Object Capture guided capture (WWDC23 session 10191). The session describes: automatic image selection by sharpness, clarity and exposure; a capture dial that shows which areas of the object have enough images and shows completion; real-time guidance on lighting (avoid dark places), movement speed (slow and smooth), distance (the object must fit in frame) and keeping the object in view; a state machine of initializing, ready, detecting, capturing, finishing, completed; a flip flow with advice on which objects to flip (rigid, texture-rich) and which not (deformable, symmetric or repetitive texture, textureless) and a recommended three passes; an ObjectCapturePointCloudView to review before processing; and a poses output giving camera position and orientation per image. [V] https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/wwdc2023/10191 . The delight of the dial is that coverage is a shape the person completes, a ring that fills, not a percentage. The point-cloud review before processing is the same instinct as #1 applied to capture.

Mapping to Recce: the dial is a template for a coverage glyph (#3) that works on a phone, on a robot operator's tablet and in the web UI. The flip advice is a model of a capture recommendation that names its reason ("symmetric texture: do not flip") instead of stating a rule.

Polycam. One app combining LiDAR, photogrammetry, Gaussian splat and non-LiDAR capture; real-time haptic and visual feedback during a walk-through; LiDAR meshes appear while scanning. [U] search snippet, https://poly.cam/blog/lidar-vs-photogrammetry-which-3d-scanning-method-is-right-for-you (the homepage host did not resolve). The pattern is haptic feedback as guidance: a buzz when coverage is thin. Whether Recce's capture companion exists is a scope question for the owner; the pattern is recorded here for that decision.

Scaniverse. Now delivered under Niantic Spatial's Capture platform: a web and mobile app, inputs from phones, 360 cameras, drones, LiDAR and robots, outputs SPZ (an open splat format), PLY, GLB and USDZ, private by default. [V] https://www.nianticspatial.com/products/capture . The page has no capture-UX detail.

KIRI Engine. Photo scan, LiDAR scan, 3D Gaussian splatting, a featureless-object mode for shiny or transparent items, quad meshes with PBR materials and AI auto-rigging. [V] https://www.kiriengine.app/ . The featureless-object mode is a named response to a known failure; Recce's failure explanations (#2, #4) name the failure the same way.

Luma. The fetched homepage now presents video-generation products (Ray 3.2, Uni-1, Luma Skills) and an Open Physical AI Lab. [V] https://lumalabs.ai/ . The page offers no capture-UX detail.

RealityScan and Reality Composer. Both fetches failed (HTTP 403 and 404). Nothing is claimed.

docs.title: 5. Craft in design and productivity tools
docs.text:
Linear. The 2024 redesign moved theme generation from HSL to LCH ("perceptually uniform", so a red and a yellow at lightness 50 look equally light) and cut 98 variables per theme to three: base colour, accent colour and contrast, with high-contrast variants. The work took about six weeks. [V] https://linear.app/now/how-we-redesigned-the-linear-ui . Two direct transfers. The frame's tokens should be generated from three inputs, which keeps the calm register consistent and gives a high-contrast theme at no cost. Every colour ramp in the scene (coverage, confidence) should be built in a perceptually uniform space so equal steps look equal; that is a correctness requirement for an honest uncertainty display, not decoration.

Raycast. A keyboard-first launcher with a command palette, more than 1,000 extensions and built-in AI chat. [V] https://www.raycast.com/ . Rerun, below, also ships a command palette. A palette lets Recce expose every action (go to stage, compare recipes, show gaps, narrate) without growing the chrome, and the same verb list is the MCP tool list: one vocabulary for people and agents.

Figma. The Figma blog's current themes: an agent now present in FigJam and Slides (the page dates the expansion to November 2026), code layers that put working prototypes on the canvas, 3D transforms combined with motion. [V] https://www.figma.com/blog/ . The pattern is the agent living where the work is, on the canvas, and its output remaining editable objects. [U] From memory, Figma's named multiplayer cursors and comment pins anchored to a spot on the canvas are the model for anchored notes on a 3D point.

Arc and Dia. Dia has an assistant in the address bar and sidebar that chats about open tabs, saved prompts called Skills, and a stated plan to bring Arc's sidebar back. [U] search snippet, https://techcrunch.com/2025/11/03/dias-ai-browser-starts-adding-arcs-greatest-hits-to-its-feature-set . The concept is the assistant that sees what the person sees. Recce's agent receives the current view, selection and time cursor as context.

Things. Not fetched. [U] No claim made.

visionOS. The HIG page lists windows, glass material, ornaments, depth, eye and hand input and comfort as the design elements. [V] https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/designing-for-visionos (summary level only). Two ideas to carry from memory, both unconfirmed here: [U] glass lets the world show through the panel, so panels over a 3D scene could keep the scene legible behind them; [U] ornaments attach controls to the edge of an object instead of floating in a toolbar, which suggests per-object controls that sit beside the selected cluster.

docs.title: 6. Engineering and high-tech visualisation
docs.text:
Rerun. The viewer is built from a Blueprint panel (what is shown and how), a Selection panel (details and configuration of the selected item), a Timeline panel that "gives you controls over what point in time you're looking at on which timeline for the rest of the viewer", and a viewport of arrangeable Views. A command palette opens with Cmd/Ctrl+K, and views carry an info icon that reveals usage guidance on hover. [V] https://rerun.io/docs/reference/viewer/overview . Timelines are plural: log time by default, a log tick opt-in, and custom timelines added by the logger, holding only 64-bit integers (sequence, nanosecond timestamp, duration). Data logged as static belongs to every timeline, including ones not yet created, and takes precedence over temporal data. [V] https://rerun.io/docs/concepts/timelines . Recce maps this directly. A run has several timelines (photo order, capture time, registration order, iteration of bundle adjustment), and the person picks which one drives the scene. Camera intrinsics and the scale reference are static data valid at every time. The existing frame already follows robotics-lab's Rerun-like look; this research adds the plural timelines and the static layer as concrete mechanics.

Foxglove. "20+ panels on one synchronized timeline" including point clouds, camera feeds, transforms and plots; semantic search over image and video topics with text prompts; saved prompts that run as agents on webhooks or schedules. [V] https://foxglove.dev/ . Panel docs: drag and drop topics onto a panel for instant visualisation, a purple border for the selected panel, panel settings as importable JSON. [V] https://docs.foxglove.dev/docs/visualization/panels/introduction . Recce's mapping: scene, photo strip, match graph and residual plot share one time cursor, so scrubbing registration moves all four. Semantic search by prompt over the photo set ("photos that look at the stern") reuses the Final Cut search idea.

Cesium. Streams 3D Tiles (buildings, photogrammetry, point clouds), takes CZML and GeoJSON, offers first-class time-dynamic visualisation "for simulations, real-time telemetry, and 4D", and switches among 3D, 2D and 2.5D Columbus views. [V] https://cesium.com/platform/cesiumjs/ . Photogrammetry arrives as 3D Tiles, so Recce's export is a Cesium input; the concept to take is time-dynamic as a first-class dimension, which a run replay (#1) is.

NASA Eyes. Browser apps for the solar system (time controls over 1950 to 2050 with fast-forward and rewind, 150 missions), asteroids (30,000 near-Earth objects), Earth (carbon dioxide, ozone, sea level), exoplanets (5,500 systems), DSN Now (real-time spacecraft links), and Mars 2020 EDL (a landing simulation). [V] https://science.nasa.gov/eyes/ . The concept is real data wrapped in a play-and-scrub frame with a time range the person can see the edges of. The EDL app is a replay of a single critical event, the model for a "replay the moment registration broke" shortcut.

NVIDIA Omniverse. Modular libraries on OpenUSD, SimReady validation that checks an asset against simulation requirements before use, RTX sensor output (camera, lidar, radar), freely available for development and production as of May 2026. [V] https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/omniverse/ . SimReady is the pattern for a readiness check: an asset passes or fails named requirements before it enters a downstream use. Recce's quality report for a robotics or survey consumer is the same shape: "scale known, frame known, coverage at least X, ready for use Y".

Flightradar24, Google Earth, Tesla, F1 telemetry, Palantir, robotics fleet UIs. The Flightradar24 blog and the Palantir Gotham page returned nothing usable (HTTP 403 and an empty summary), the F1 fetch redirected to the homepage, and Google Earth, Tesla and fleet UIs were not fetched. Everything below is [U], from memory. [U] Flightradar24 pairs a live map with a playback slider and a trail behind each aircraft, so recent history is drawn as a fading line; the matching Recce idea is a fading trail behind each camera showing where it was before bundle adjustment moved it. [U] F1 broadcast graphics pair a speed trace with a position on the track map, and call out one number against a reference lap; the matching idea is a delta against a reference recipe, drawn on the scene. [U] Tesla's in-car view renders only what the sensors believe is there, including ghosted objects when confidence is low; this is the direct precedent for #4. [U] Situational displays in the Palantir style centre an object-and-link graph with a map and a timeline; the matching idea is the match graph (#2) as a linked panel next to the scene.

docs.title: 7. Explanatory and interactive work
docs.text:
Bartosz Ciechanowski. The most recent article on his index is "Moon" (17 December 2024), built from draggable 3D simulators where the reader moves bodies and changes velocities, time-scrubbing sliders, camera controls that lock on a body or orbit freely, parameter sliders for mass, distance and eccentricity, side-by-side space and surface views, and an observer figurine the reader places anywhere on Earth. [V] https://ciechanow.ski/ . The index may be dated; newer articles may exist that the fetch did not show. The concepts to take: each diagram has one or two controls, the same object is shown from two viewpoints at once, and the reader's finger is the instrument. Recce mapping: a "why triangulation needs a baseline" explainer where the reader drags two camera icons apart and the uncertainty ellipsoid of a point shrinks; a second view shows the same point from above. Each such mini-lab lives next to the term it explains in the inspector.

Distill. The momentum article uses sliders for step size and momentum with live phase diagrams, an error decomposition per eigenvalue animated as parameters change, and side-by-side loss curves of two methods. [V] https://distill.pub/2017/momentum/ . Distill ran from 2016 to 2021 and is on an indefinite hiatus; its stated belief is that "reactive diagrams allow for a type of communication not possible in static mediums". [V] https://distill.pub/about/ . The pattern for #6: two curves from two recipes on shared axes with the parameter that separates them under the reader's hand.

Bret Victor, Learnable Programming. Principles stated on the page: show the data; make meaning transparent (labels on hover, annotations connecting code to output); visualise flow over time so the reader scrubs execution; eliminate hidden state or make it visible; create by reacting, starting from something visible and adjusting; move from concrete to abstract in small steps. [V] https://worrydream.com/LearnableProgramming/ . These six apply nearly line for line. Show the data: the match is a line, not a count. Hidden state: the intermediate pose estimate after each iteration is drawn, because the engine's belief at step k is the hidden state of a reconstruction. Scrub: #1. Concrete to abstract: the first explanation of coverage is one photo's frustum, then two, then the whole set.

Nicky Case. Explorable explanations including The Evolution of Trust and a tool for nested, expandable explanations (Nutshell), all under a public-domain waiver. [V] https://ncase.me/ . Nutshell's idea, an explanation that expands inline inside a sentence, fits a debrief (#5): a sentence says "twelve photos hold the left side" and the phrase opens to show them, with no navigation away.

3Blue1Brown. The newest lesson as of today is dated 17 November 2026 (compression and arithmetic coding). [V] https://www.3blue1brown.com/ . The page says nothing about method. [U] From memory, the lessons are built in the author's Manim library and rely on one persistent visual object transformed step by step; the lesson for Recce is object permanence, so the cloud on screen at step k is the same object as at step k-1, morphing, never cut.

Observable and the Pudding (scrollytelling). The Observable homepage returned HTTP 429 and the Pudding process page returned 404. [U] From memory, scrollytelling binds a sticky scene to scroll position so each paragraph triggers a camera move or a state change; it is the delivery form of #7 (a presentation is a scroll or a click path through camera positions) and of a shareable debrief page.

docs.title: 8. AI-native and multimodal UX
docs.text:
Evidence from this pass: Spline's MCP (agents read the scene, write changes, frame views, and the human keeps editing in the same file) [V] https://spline.design/ ; Figma's agent arriving in more canvases and producing editable layers [V] https://www.figma.com/blog/ ; Foxglove's semantic search and saved-prompt agents [V] https://foxglove.dev/ ; Flow Studio's 3D Editor, which puts a spatial step before generation [V] https://digitalproduction.com/2026/08/04/autodesk-flow-studio-adds-3d-editor-and-canvas/ (trade press); Dia's assistant that reads open tabs [U] https://techcrunch.com/2025/11/03/dias-ai-browser-starts-adding-arcs-greatest-hits-to-its-feature-set . No page fetched in this pass documents a product that shows an agent's evidence as clickable citations; that pattern comes from memory ([U]: search products that attach numbered sources to claims, and coding agents that show tool calls as a collapsible log). It is the central pattern for #5 and appears in the ranked table as an adopted rule, not a copied feature: every sentence in a debrief carries a handle to the photos, matches or numbers behind it, and activating the handle moves the camera there.

Rules distilled from the V items above for the agent face:

  1. The agent edits the shared scene, not a copy (Spline).
  2. Its output stays editable and deletable (Figma).
  3. It receives the current selection and time cursor as context (Dia, [U]).
  4. It states the cost of a step before it runs (Flow Studio credits, [V] Autodesk blog above).
  5. It searches the photo set by meaning (Foxglove).

docs.title: Patterns worth stealing
docs.text:
Ranked by expected effect on the "wow" and the understanding, then by cost.

Rank Pattern Source What it does in Recce Idea 1 One shared time cursor driving every panel, with plural timelines and a static layer Rerun, Foxglove [V] Scrubbing registration moves scene, photo strip, match graph and residual plot together; the person chooses photo order, capture time or iteration as the axis #1, NEW 1 2 Completion ring for coverage Apple capture dial [V] A ring or sphere glyph that fills as angles are covered; works on a phone, a tablet, the web UI #3, NEW 5 3 Every claim carries a clickable handle to its evidence Agent UX pattern [U], Spline MCP [V] A debrief sentence opens its photos and matches and flies the camera there #5, NEW 2 4 Show hidden state, scrub flow, concrete to abstract Bret Victor [V] The engine's pose belief after each iteration is drawn; explanations build from one frustum to the full set #1, #2, NEW 3 5 Reader-driven mini-lab beside a term Ciechanowski, Distill [V] Drag two cameras apart and watch a point's uncertainty ellipsoid shrink; one control, two viewpoints #4, NEW 4 6 Analysis as overlay with one toggle each Halide zebras and peaking [U], Forma layers [U] Coverage and confidence laid over the scene as toggleable overlays that never replace it #3, #4 7 Perceptually uniform colour ramps and a three-input theme Linear [V] Coverage and confidence ramps built in LCH, so equal data steps look equal; frame tokens from base, accent and contrast #3, #4, NEW 6 8 Recipe as a node network with swap-in-place Houdini [V], Blender Swap Node [V] Compare two recipes by the node whose parameter differs; swap a strategy and keep its connections #6 9 Command palette with one verb list for people and agents Raycast, Rerun [V] Cmd+K reaches every action; the same verbs form the MCP tool list NEW 7 10 Drill in with breadcrumbs, double-click to enter Blender 5.0 [V] Run, stage, step navigation without losing place #1 11 Soft blending as the default Womp [V] Uncertainty rendered as a field that merges between cameras, not a patchwork #4 12 Inline expandable explanation Nutshell (Nicky Case) [V] A phrase in the debrief opens in place to show the photos #5 13 Readiness check against named requirements Omniverse SimReady [V] The quality report states "ready for use Y" with the requirements it checked NEW 8 14 Browser review link, no install Shapr3D [V] A read-only link to a presentation scene #7 15 Reduce Motion switch Blender 5.0 [V] Required once #1 animates by default #1 16 Fading trail behind a moving object Flightradar24 [U] Camera positions before and after bundle adjustment as a fading trail #1 17 Compare as a wipe on one view Resolve still store [U] The split slider already in #6, with a reference lap style delta #6 18 Tethered live result Capture One [V] A streaming capture session registers each frame within seconds NEW 9

docs.title: New ideas
docs.text:
These are suggestions beyond the eight in visual ideas, each a direction to mock, not a decision.

  1. Plural timelines. The run has a timeline per axis (photo order, capture time, registration order, optimiser iteration), a picker chooses which drives the scene, and static facts (intrinsics, scale reference) belong to all of them. Source: Rerun [V].
  2. Evidence handles. Each sentence and each number in a debrief or report has a handle. Activating it selects the underlying photos or matches in the scene and flies the camera. A sentence without a handle is flagged in the report as an unsupported claim. Source: agent pattern [U], Spline [V].
  3. The engine's belief at step k. A scrubbable view of what the engine believed at each iteration, including poses it later discarded. Source: Bret Victor, hidden state [V].
  4. Mini-labs. A short set of reader-driven demonstrations (baseline and triangulation, overlap and match count, blur and feature count, rolling shutter and straight lines, refraction and apparent focal length) embedded beside the term in the inspector, each with one or two controls. Source: Ciechanowski, Distill [V].
  5. A shared coverage glyph. One ring or sphere glyph drawn identically in the web UI, a phone companion and an operator tablet, so a person who learned it on one surface reads it on the others. Source: Apple capture dial [V].
  6. Honest colour. A rule that every ramp in the scene is perceptually uniform, with a colour-blind-safe variant and a luminance-only fallback, and a "what does this colour mean" legend that opens from any overlay. Source: Linear [V].
  7. One verb list. A single registry of actions powers the command palette, the CLI subcommands, the HTTP routes and the MCP tools. Source: Raycast, Rerun [V]; the registry itself is a design inference, not copied.
  8. Readiness stamps. The quality report ends with named downstream uses (survey, robot localisation, print, web viewing) and a pass, fail or unknown for each against stated requirements. Source: Omniverse SimReady [V].
  9. Live registration during capture. For a streaming source, each arriving frame registers into the model in view; a frame that fails to register is shown as a ghost at its expected pose. Source: Capture One tethering [V], Apple point-cloud preview [V].
  10. The agent as a scene editor. The agent places ghost cameras, labels and a camera path directly into the scene through MCP, and the person moves or deletes them. Source: Spline [V].
  11. Replay the moment. One click replays the few iterations around the registration step with the largest residual jump. Source: NASA Eyes EDL replay [V], Flightradar24 playback [U].
  12. Frame the cost. Every recipe shows a time and energy estimate before it runs and the measured figure after. Source: Flow Studio credits [V].

docs.title: Not covered
docs.text:
What the pass did not check, and why. Treat every item as an open lead.

Pages that failed or returned nothing usable:

  • Autodesk University 2026 announcements (HTTP 403), the Autodesk neural CAD article (403), the Forma environmental-analysis page (403), the Revit Forma wind analysis page (not fetched). Forma, neural CAD and Bernini rest on search snippets only.
  • Blender's own 5.0 release page (403) and the CG Channel Blender review (403); the Blender claims rest on the developer release notes only, which cover the UI and not the headline features.
  • Unreal Engine 5.7 release notes (403): no UE editor claim of any kind. Unreal's Sequencer, MegaLights and editor mode changes are unchecked.
  • RealityScan (403), Reality Composer (404), Apple's ObjectCaptureSession documentation page (it returned a title only) and the Apple Object Capture capture-guidance article (404).
  • Polycam (host did not resolve): capture guidance rests on one snippet. Scaniverse's own capture UX (its page redirected to an enterprise product page with no UX detail). Luma's capture product (the page now shows video generation).
  • Observable (HTTP 429), the Pudding (404), Palantir Gotham (empty summary), the F1 page (redirect, not followed), Flightradar24's blog (403), Halide's own page (404) and the Rerun blueprint page (404).

Arenas or items not attempted:

  • Darkroom, Things, Tesla visualisation, Google Earth, robotics fleet UIs, the Houdini viewport and spreadsheet behaviour, Capture One layers and styles, Lightroom's before and after modes, Resolve scopes, Maya and 3ds Max UX changes, Fusion's UX, Shapr3D's Apple Pencil gestures, Nomad's gestures, Spline's AI generation, Arc's boosts, 3Blue1Brown's tooling (all from memory where mentioned, otherwise absent).
  • Bartosz Ciechanowski's articles other than the index summary; the summary may predate newer articles. No Distill article beyond momentum.
  • Whether any shipping product shows agent evidence as clickable citations inside a 3D scene. The nearest finding is Spline's MCP, which does not cite evidence.

Limits of method:

  • Every [V] came through a model-generated summary of the fetched page, not a raw read. Counts, names and dates are likelier to be right than the nuance of a phrase. Trade-press items (Flow Studio 3D Editor) report on the vendor and are not the vendor's own words.
  • No product was run, so every statement about delight is an inference from a description, not an observation of use. No video, motion or interaction was seen; patterns such as the capture dial and Rerun's timeline are known only as text.
  • Nothing here was tested against Recce's data. RC-P6 is the place to test any of these on the ETH3D kicker scene; the mini-lab, evidence-handle and plural-timeline ideas need a mock before a UX spec.
  • No claim was made about licensing. Several sources (Spline, Foxglove, Omniverse, Resolve) are proprietary; Rerun and Cesium are open source, and Recce takes concepts from all of them, not code.
  • The search tool is US-only and reported results as of today; snippets can be stale.

docs.title: Review of the concept-phase start (2026-11-23)
docs.text: An independent advisor review (Fable 5.1, read-only) of the brief, the architecture sketch, the use cases, the research notes and the reference documents, as they stood on 2026-11-23. Condensed; the full findings are below by heading. External facts the reviewer did not check are marked (unverified).

docs.title: Status of the findings
docs.text: Finding Status Laptop "complete system" contradicts the platform matrix Fixed 2026-11-23 (brief §1, sketch §4, open question 16) Splats in the MVP: brief and sketch vs product analysis Fixed 2026-11-23 (superseded note in the product analysis) iPhone app vs non-goals and stale "later" text Fixed 2026-11-23 (brief §2 and §4, sketch §1, use cases UC-A1) Competitive gap overstated Fixed 2026-11-23 (brief §3) Prototype restructuring (merge P1/P2, drop iMac Pro, P3 onto a large set, testable criteria, own robot fixture, Chemigram route in the develop prototype, underwater criterion) Done 2026-11-24 (brief §5, new numbering) Positioning Partly answered 2026-11-24: origin and drivers in brief §0; vision sentence recorded as a candidate Licence Decided 2026-11-24: MIT from the start (Licensing) Capture-set amendments, storage budget, privacy of traces, proposed tolerances Open — with the owner

docs.title: 1. Gaps
docs.text:
1. "The laptop alone is a complete system" is false with the default stack: no COLMAP dense or gsplat on the M4 Pro (tools overview §18).
  2. RC-P3 tests the wrong input: fanning out features and matching on 60–150 iPhone photos takes seconds, so transfer dominates. The hours on large sets are dense depth and splat training, which run on one or two machines (GB10, X3 if HIP works). The riskiest unknowns — cutting and merging a view graph across machines (sketch Q5) and the X3 HIP dense build — are untested. "Matches a single-machine run" needs a tolerance: GPU SIFT is not bit-identical across CUDA, HIP and CPU.
  3. Splats in or out of the MVP: documents disagreed.
  4. The iPhone app contradicted the non-goals and stale "later" text in four places.
  5. Prototype dependencies inverted: RC-P4 needs ARKit poses (RC-P10 or a third-party export) and MapAnything on CUDA (the GB10 build RC-P2 proves); RC-P5 depends on a Gazebo fixture robotics-lab has offered but not built.
  6. Untestable criteria: RC-P6 ("the owner agrees"), RC-P7 ("usable"), RC-P5 and RC-P9 ("a stated tolerance", none stated); RC-P8 has none. Suggested RC-P6 test: remove a region's images, the agent names the region, add them back, show the coverage metric moved.
  7. The capture-set format cannot yet carry an iPhone capture: per-sensor intrinsics (ARKit's vary per frame with focus (unverified)), PNG-only images (no DNG or HEIC), no specified conversion from ARKit's y-up camera-to-world frame.
  8. No data-volume or storage budget: 150 D850/A1 RAWs is about 8 GB before intermediates, depth maps and caches on every worker. Deletion by hash must also purge worker and rented-box caches.
  9. Four GPU platforms is an unpriced maintenance tax; the iMac Pro costs more than it contributes.
  10. The competitive gap was overstated (WebODM, Meshroom, Brush, RealityScan with AMD; splats exist in Pix4D, Polycam, KIRI, Postshot, WebODM).
  11. Decided early without evidence: own worker protocol, SvelteKit + three.js + Spark, monorepo, X3 as coordinator. Decided late: what the MVP delivers for which use case, and any time budget for one person.
  12. Privacy and licence: traces would carry home-scan file names; Refractive COLMAP's licence is unknown; "open source later" while licence is listed open; the benchmark set holds private photos.
  13. Minor: primer §8 says COLMAP dense needs CUDA (also HIP); primer §13 attributes the range-dependent attenuation finding to Sea-thru, which applies Akkaynak and Treibitz's 2018 revised model (unverified detail).

docs.title: 2. Motivation and positioning
docs.text:
1. As a Metashape or RealityScan replacement it is not worth building; for objects, bikes and rooms free tools suffice (RealityScan Windows-only unverified).
  2. What no tool does: scale, frame and uncertainty as an output contract; quality as machine-readable state with per-image verdicts and coverage regions; robot or ARKit poses as weighted priors with a refinement statement; refraction and range-based colour.
  3. Three equal pillars is a lack of focus. The hardware pool is mostly an engineering itch for small sets; its real value is "offload from the field laptop to home, burst to a rented GPU". The photographer pillar competes with free products. Robots and agents have no incumbent.
  4. Proposed centre: the scientific reconstruction model plus agent-readable quality state, with underwater as the flagship domain.
  5. MCP is substantive only if the loop closes: the engine names a weak link, an agent turns it into a capture request for a robot or a diver, the engine re-registers incrementally. Second use: agents running the benchmark across recipes.
  6. Proposed vision sentence: "A reconstruction engine that always says what it knows and what it does not (scale, frame, coverage, uncertainty) so that a person, a robot or an agent can decide what to capture next, above water and below."

docs.title: 3. Ideas for more value
docs.text:
1. Capture judge first: a CPU-only recon judge — blur, exposure and white-balance variance, overlap, lens groups, components and weak links after a fast sparse solve — as JSON and over MCP; usable at the dive site and as a front end to other tools. About 2–3 weeks.
  2. Chemigram as the develop stage: darktable headless, gray-card white balance, state propagation across a set; reverse: range maps become a Sea-thru primitive in Chemigram. Days.
  3. Open underwater benchmark with ground truth: flat vs dome port, GoPro vs DSLR, scale bars and tags; Brown vs Refractive COLMAP vs MapAnything. A research contribution; gives RC-P8 a criterion.
  4. Robotics-lab as the first real client, closing the capture-advice loop.
  5. A repeatable motorised object rig for benchmark error bars.
  6. Rerun as the engineering viewer until the product UI earns its place.
  7. 4D reef monitoring: two dives, co-registered, change detection.
  8. GoPro GPMF gravity and gyro as SfM priors.

docs.title: 4. Sequencing proposed by the reviewer
docs.text:
This week: the shoes with the iPhone and the D850 beside an AprilTag board, COLMAP and GLOMAP on the M4 Pro and the X3; in parallel the COLMAP HIP dense build on the X3 and pycolmap + gsplat on the GB10; quality.json v0 with three MCP read tools; capture-set amendments to robotics-lab.

Restructuring: cut the iMac Pro; merge P2 into P1; move P3 after a large set exists, with dense depth and SfM partition as the unit of work and a stated tolerance; defer P10 in favour of a Record3D or Polycam export; replace P5's Gazebo fixture with a Blender render; Chemigram in P7b; give P8 a criterion and move it ahead of P7.

docs.title: Questions for the owner before the vision
docs.text:
1. Which single result in three months makes the project worth it?
  2. When is the next dive, with scale bars and both port types?
  3. Has the shoes set been tried in RealityScan or Apple Object Capture?
  4. Is the hardware pillar about using every machine, or about offloading from the field and bursting to rented GPUs?
  5. Storage budget and retention rule for home scans?
  6. Will robotics-lab deliver a real capture set in the first quarter, or does this project make its own fixture?
  7. Metric tolerances for RC-P5 and RC-P9, in millimetres and as a percentage.
  8. Licence: decide permissive now, or keep it open?
  9. Is the iOS app worth the weeks it displaces?
  10. Does the GB10's shared-GPU schedule leave enough CUDA time, or is a rented card the real CUDA worker?

docs.title: Robotics-lab: what it hands over and what it expects back
docs.text: Input to the brief and to the capture-set RFC. Sources: robotics-lab's RFC-0025 §5 and §5.1 (chipi/robotics-lab, docs/rfc/RFC-0025-mvp1-to-mvp2.md; Accepted 2026-11-23, nothing built), and a message from the robotics-lab project on 2026-11-23. These are that project's requirements; this project owns its design.

docs.title: The seam
docs.text:
• Two repositories, joined by a file contract: a command line plus versioned files. Neither imports the other. Neither project writes into the other's repository.
  • Command line shape proposed there: recon --images D --manifest M --out O.
  • Manifest versioning: a reader accepts its own and older versions and refuses a newer one.
  • Agreed points get folded into RFC-0025 §5.1 by the robotics-lab project. Proposals go to it as messages, not commits.

docs.title: The capture set (proposed there, to be versioned together)
docs.text:
<capture set>/
  manifest.json      # "manifest": N; run id; frames; axes; units; clock; source run, stream, sha256 per chunk
  images/000001.png  # lossless or uncompressed stills, never lossy
  depth/000001.png   # optional; 16-bit, mm; same index as images/; 0 = no data
  images.json        # per image: file, wall_ns, sensor id, camera pose + frame + source (truth|belief), actual settings
  cameras.json       # per sensor: intrinsics, distortion, resolution, mount (camera to base); all optional
  • Exposure, gain and white balance locked for a capture; actual per-frame values recorded.
  • No processing applied: no undistortion, gamma or contrast. Colour normalisation is this project's job.
  • Poses are the camera's pose (not the robot's), nearest tick within 0.1 s; right-handed, z up, metres. Priors, not truth — except in a simulator, where source: truth is exact.
  • Wall-clock nanoseconds plus a clock epoch, so a set spanning a simulator reset is not misread.

docs.title: What it wants back
docs.text:
• A mesh, point cloud or splat in an open format (mesh.ply, cloud.ply in its diagram).
  • Known scale and a placeable frame: metric in the frame of the given poses, or an explicit transform with the scale stated. No poses in → say the scale is arbitrary. RFC-0025 calls this "the main trap".
  • provenance.json: input checksums, tool and version, parameters, frame, scale, time.
  • Poses and intrinsics optional on input; a statement of whether poses were refined, and the refined poses if so.
  • Same input and parameters → same output, as far as possible.
  • gaps.json beside provenance.json, pulled (decided 2026-11-24, recorded in robotics-lab's RFC-0025 §5.1, "The gap list"; design in gap-list interface).

docs.title: Settled since (2026-11-24)
docs.text: The project is named Recce (this repository, chipi/recce); the licence is MIT. A Recce model may feed a Gazebo world: robotics-lab designs the import in its MVP 2 (its RFC-0025 Q21). The manifest gains site and targets; frame identity is robotics-lab's to mint, one id per map of a site; capture is triggered by a capture_view goal kind after the Burger's cameras. Details in the gap-list interface, "The operator's decisions".

docs.title: Left open for this project
docs.text: Splat, mesh and point-cloud formats; colour normalisation; capture needs (overlap, speed, blur, frame count) — robotics-lab wants these as input to how a robot drives a capture; where it runs and how large a set may be (uncompressed 640×480 at 30 Hz is about 1.7 GB per minute); how a result is placed into its frames; whether a model is ever used by a mapper or a judge (a pleasing model is not collision-safe). Privacy: home scans hold faces, screens and documents, so retention matters.

docs.title: Robotics-lab today
docs.text:
• No real camera images exist yet. The Microduck is simulated (MuJoCo, 8×8 ToF depth, IMU, odometry; its "camera" is a stand-in recogniser). The NXT has no camera.
  • MVP 2 is a TurtleBot3 Burger on ROS 2 Jazzy, Gazebo first; the real robot's first upgrade is an RGB camera plus a depth camera, model not chosen. The only measured stream is 640×480 at 30 Hz in Gazebo.
  • Runs are MCAP (format 2); image streams live in companion streams/<id>.mcap files.
  • Viewers: Rerun 0.43.2, Lichtblick, three.js (STL meshes). Nothing there reads PLY, glTF or splats yet; Rerun has unused Mesh3D and GaussianSplats3D archetypes.
  • Offered: a Gazebo capture set with exact poses as an early test fixture.

docs.title: Step 0 close-out report (2026-11-27)
docs.text: The input to RC-01 Vision. It states what Step 0 set out to prove, what it proved and did not, what the mock-ups settled, and what carries into the build. The numbers come from Step 0 status and findings and from each prototype's and mock-up's README, which hold the full results and their "Not covered" lists; this report adds no new measurement.

docs.title: What Step 0 set out to do
docs.text: Two tracks ran side by side (brief §5). The prototypes (RC-P1 to RC-P13) prove how the technology works; a prototype counts as proven when it meets its stated criterion, and a failure with its evidence is also a result. The mock-ups (RC-M1 to RC-M8) work out how the product looks and behaves; a mock-up is done when the owner has judged its concepts on screen. Step 0 ends when the mock-ups have the owner's verdicts and this report is written (owner, 2026-11-27). Everything ran on public datasets with published references; the owner's own captures and the friend's dive set come after.

docs.title: What the evidence says about the vision
docs.text:
The vision sentence under consideration in the brief is: "A reconstruction engine that always says what it knows and what it does not — scale, frame, coverage, uncertainty — so that a person, a robot or an agent can decide what to capture next, above water and below." Step 0 tested each part of it.

Scale comes from priors and references, never from pixels alone. With exact poses a robot's set lands within 0.021% scale (RC-P9); RTK priors on half a drone's photos fix scale to +0.025% (RC-P8, RC-P13); a learned model's metric scale is off by up to 41% (RC-P8), so it never sets scale. A photos-only reconstruction has no scale, and the mock-ups say so on screen (RC-M1's "scale: arbitrary"). The drone and building segments show a second limit: a focal length 0.6–1.3% long trades against flying height, so the surface reads 0.3–1.1 m low until control points or a calibrated lens pin it.

Frame is a contract that can be checked. The robot set's axes, handedness and quaternion order are verified by render, and both wrong conventions fail (RC-P9).

Coverage predicts error, and an agent can read it. On RC-P10's room, surfaces no frame saw are 52.4 mm from the Faro scan and those seen by 32 or more frames 14.7 mm (RC-M2). An agent with read tools finds a held-out region (RC-P3). Where to stand next is the engine's job: an agent inventing positions put 0 of 3 shots where a photographer can stand, and 3 of 3 with the engine's spots (RC-M3).

Uncertainty can be carried per element. A structured model tags every wall, floor and passage as measured, inferred or unknown with its sigma (RC-P13); the room meets its reference on every measured dimension and marks 1.92 m² of floor it never saw as unknown, not guessed.

Underwater is a scale problem first. A pinhole calibration through a flat port misses scale by up to 4.8% depending on where the object is; a refractive model holds ±0.28% (RC-P12). Colour needs the RAW: the published TIFs clip red to zero on 78–99.9% of pixels. The cast at 6–19 m is one global tint; what changes with range is contrast, which the simple backscatter fit restores unevenly.

The central bet is not yet tested. That splitting the work across machines and a rented GPU beats the best single machine (RC-P7) is the reason the project exists, and Step 0 did not run it. What exists is the ground under it: the same registration on three machines and three architectures (RC-P1), dense depth on CUDA and HIP (RC-P2), and the measurement that dense depth and a splat together need up to 50 GB of GPU memory.

docs.title: The seven complaints, first numbers
docs.text:
The brief turns each of the owner's complaints into a measurement (§0). Each now has a first number (RC-P4, RC-P12):

Complaint First number Blurry, smeared textures A texel covers a median 10.2 mm on seen faces; 89% of the textured area comes from one photo Noisy or melted geometry Courtyard F1 at 5 cm: 0.35 from our poses, 0.88 from ground-truth poses; poses decide dense quality Holes 16% of the courtyard mesh's faces are seen by no photo Colour seams Median ΔE 2.48 across seams against 2.14 inside patches Wrong colour underwater Grey patches a median 31.1° from grey with the camera's white balance, 1.4° after one white balance on the RAW (15 charts, 6–19 m) Untrustworthy scale Pinhole underwater up to −4.8%; learned metric scale up to 41% off; robot priors 0.021% Slow GLOMAP maps 3–4 times faster than COLMAP; dense depth 1,169 s (GB10, CUDA) against 3,205 s (X3, HIP)

docs.title: What the mock-ups settled
docs.text:
Seven mock-ups were built on real prototype output, except RC-M5, which is synthetic by design. The owner kept every concept of RC-M1 to RC-M7, the coach on RC-M1 and RC-M2 included; what goes into the product is decided when the build starts. The patterns they share (visual ideas):

  • The reconstruction as a story with evidence (RC-M1, RC-M3): the run replayed camera by camera, a debrief whose every claim opens its evidence in the scene, and a claim without evidence flagged.
  • Quality on the surface (RC-M2): light and shadow by how many frames saw a surface, confidence as solid or hatched, the reference beside the estimate where one exists.
  • The gap list as the brief for the next capture (RC-M1): each gap with where to stand, what to shoot and why, a site map, and the same list as JSON for a robot.
  • Recipes as node graphs, compared by the node that differs, with cost estimated before and measured after (RC-M4).
  • A presentation that stays honest (RC-M6): a path through the photos, the splat where it holds and the mesh where it does not, and an "About this model" card on every shared link.
  • Underwater made visible (RC-M7): the water's colour against each correction, and the refraction as a lens that can be switched off.
  • A camera is its photo: every scene draws a camera as its image where it was taken.
  • AI is optional, and a coach when present (owner, 2026-11-27): every view works from geometry and rules alone; with the person's own AI connected it explains why, orders a plan from the engine's own actions, says how to know it worked and what the facts cannot say, and every number it writes is checked against the fact it cites. One recorded call each on RC-M1, M2 and M7 cost US\(0.038–0.082; RC-M5's five tutor calls cost US\)0.083 together. Unsupported statements per mock-up: 0 (RC-M1, RC-M7), 1 (RC-M2), 3 of 51 (RC-M5). One wrong statement without a number got through on RC-M1; the checker cannot catch such a statement.
  • What an AI call costs depends on its context, not its prompt: the same call cost US\(1.75 with an agent's default context and US\)0.028 without it (RC-M4).

docs.title: Decided by the owner during Step 0
docs.text:
• AI is optional; Recce is complete without it, and is an MCP server for a person's own agent (2026-11-27).
  • The learned route is an optional second route beside COLMAP, kept only after the agreement check, never the source of scale (RC-P8).
  • Recipes, per-device corrections and tuned settings live in a separate private repository; the public engine keeps them separable (2026-11-26).
  • RC-P7 moves to the build phase; RC-P10 stays not proven with its cause recorded, pose refinement moves to the build; RC-P13 closes partly proven; the cave tolerance is 2% or 5 cm (2026-11-26 and 2026-11-27).
  • The underwater benchmark capture is decided after the rest of Step 0 (2026-11-26).

The UI stack is decided on the mock-ups' evidence

docs.title: What RC-01 Vision can take from this
docs.text:
These are proposals for the owner, drawn from the evidence above:

  • The vision sentence holds as written: each of its parts (scale, frame, coverage, uncertainty, the next capture, above water and below) has a working first result.
  • Scale is stated, never inferred: from priors, references or control points, or reported as arbitrary. A learned model may propose poses; it never sets scale.
  • The engine supplies positions, numbers and verdicts; an AI explains, orders and coaches, and is checked against the engine.
  • Distribution remains untested; where it sits in the build's order is open.

Decided by the owner after this report (2026-11-27): the first case is the owner's home with the iPhone app, objects first and then a whole room, leading into the robot cases; learn mode is a feature inside the product. Both are recorded in the brief §4.

docs.title: Not covered
docs.text:
• Public data only. No owner capture and no dive set; one scene per prototype in several cases (RC-P5 on pipes, RC-P9 on its fixture, RC-P12 on one site and one rig).
  • This report summarises; it does not re-run or re-check any number. The prototype READMEs are authoritative.
  • Mock-up verdicts are on concepts, not on finished design; RC-M2 to RC-M7 had one phase each.
  • No cost model for a full capture end to end: per-stage times exist for single scenes, not for a 1,500-photo set.
