docs.title: Findings
docs.text:
Strategies. On three scenes and three machines GLOMAP maps 3–4 times faster than COLMAP's incremental mapper with the same pose accuracy (rotation within a few tenths of a degree, position under a centimetre apart). GLOMAP's reprojection error is about twice COLMAP's on every scene and machine (1.9–2.9 px against 1.1–1.3 px); the cause is not known.

Scoring. A camera a mapper poses without any 3D point is not part of the model. GLOMAP posed one such photo on kicker about 47 m from its true place, and including it in the alignment turned a 0.6° result into 13°. Every score now counts only cameras that hold points.

Machines and builds. - pycolmap 4.2.1 from PyPI has no CUDA and no Linux ARM wheel. On the GB10 the conda-forge build (CUDA) is used through micromamba. It runs SIFT extraction and matching on the GPU, about three times faster than the CPU on the X3 or the M4 Pro. - Runs on different machines give the same quality but not identical models: GLOMAP joined kicker's problem photo on the M4 Pro and the GB10, not on the X3. - Registration of a 38-image scene peaks at 28 GB resident memory (courtyard, M4 Pro). - Poisson meshing in the conda-forge pycolmap build for the GB10 aborts ("Failed to close loop"), even on a synthetic sphere. Delaunay meshing works and is used. - COLMAP upstream has a HIP backend since 2026-10 (PR #4795). Built from main in a ROCm 7.2.4 container for gfx1151, it runs dense depth on the X3 at about 2.7 times the GB10's time, at 98% GPU use; one run aborted with a memory-aperture violation and a repeat passed (not root-caused). Nothing is installed on the host.

GB10 GPU time. The DGX serves production LLMs in gpu-mode prod, which leaves about 15 GB of memory. Recce GPU work runs in a free window: by day under the owner's standing go, switched by the Recce session as markodragoljevic, switched back to prod and verified by the homelab session. Dense depth and a splat together used up to 50 GB.

Quality state. Coverage per region is enough for an agent to find a removed region, when the removal is local: choosing the region whose removal touches the fewest neighbours matters, since a naive choice left 12 of 22 regions at zero coverage and the test unanswerable.

RAW. A minimal pipeline (rawpy, one white balance and one exposure for the whole set) registers as well as the camera JPEGs, with the most even colour. Chemigram, as driven here, registered 7 of 14 photos with dark, yellow-green renders; stock darktable on the same RAW files is neutral, so the cause lies in Chemigram's presets or the recipe used. Not investigated.

Robot capture sets. With exact poses the model lands within 0.021% scale and 0.18% placement; the frame conversion (OpenGL camera axes, z-up world, {x, y, z, w} quaternions) is checked by render, and both wrong-convention controls fail.

Poses decide dense quality. On courtyard the same dense stage scores F1 0.35 at 5 cm from RC-P1's poses and 0.88 from ETH3D's ground-truth poses; RC-P1's cameras sit a median 6.1 cm from the truth after alignment. Pose refinement before dense is the first lever, ahead of any dense setting. Why RC-P1's poses are that far off is not investigated.

Splat quality. gsplat at 30,000 steps reaches PSNR 27.7 on Mip-NeRF 360 garden and 29.2 on counter, in line with published gsplat figures. On courtyard (7,000 steps) it stays low: 18.4 dB from RC-P1's poses, 20.9 from ground-truth poses, so poses explain part of it; 30,000 steps from RC-P1's poses give 18.2 dB, so the step count does not. Garden used 14.3 GiB of GPU memory, close to what prod mode leaves free.

Texture. texrecon (BSD; dependencies BSD and MPL-2.0) textures the courtyard mesh in 52 s on the GB10; 16% of the faces are seen by no photo.

Learned poses. MapAnything's Apache checkpoint alone is 0.9–1.7° and 12–37 cm off on ETH3D; bundle-adjusted from the same SIFT matches it comes close to COLMAP (0.36–0.82° relative against 0.40–0.69°). The adjustment lets the scale drift (−41% and −74% on two ETH3D runs), so the adjusted model is anchored to MapAnything's camera centres. On ARKitScenes it fails on one low-texture video (82° relative) and is wrong in parts on a textured one; COLMAP registers 10–18% of the frames of the low-texture videos. MapAnything needs 42–59 GiB of GPU memory for 90–218 views, more than prod mode leaves. The agreement check (learned against each COLMAP component, within 2° relative rotation and 2% of extent, no ground truth) passes all six ETH3D runs and rejects every broken learned model; its one miss is a COLMAP component that is itself 13.8° off. It can confirm the learned model only where COLMAP also registered, and on these runs the frames only the learned model has are where it fails.

Underwater. Refraction is a scale error, not noise: on AquaMVS a pinhole calibration is off by −0.03% to −4.8% depending on where the board is, and a refractive model by at most ±0.28%. Colour underwater needs the RAW: SQUID's published TIFs clip red to zero on 78–99.9% of pixels. Over 6–19 m on the Satil wreck the colour cast is nearly one global tint, which a single white balance removes; what changes with range is contrast (0.39 to 0.07 on the grey ramp), and the simple per-image backscatter fit restores it unevenly, whichever model is fitted (simple or Sea-thru's form): near the camera the deck holds no dark objects, so the dark-pixel estimate overshoots. Our own pipeline gets no depth from SQUID's few hazy stereo pairs without the rig calibration. SQUID's chart annotations sit a few pixels off its published undistorted images and are snapped before use.

Without AI (the default): the engine writes the debrief from templates and rules, every number with its tool call, and places each new shot by a where-to-stand rule (hand height, walked area, facing side, clear sight, a new angle). With the person's own AI connected (opt-in, OpenAI-compatible endpoint): the AI adds what the model is good for, priorities per purpose and a walking plan above the engine's text, checked by replay. An agent left to invent positions put 0 of 3 shots where a photographer can stand; with the engine's spots, 3 of 3. Owner verdict (2026-11-27): all concepts kept RC-M4 recipes and comparison Phase 1 built 2026-11-27 on ETH3D kicker and courtyard: the recipe graph forked at the node that differs (mapping), a wipe across one 3D view, what changed with a verdict by rule (or by the person's own AI, checked), and cost per stage estimated before and measured after, time and energy (the X3's package power above idle). GLOMAP maps 3.4–3.7 times faster for a quarter to two fifths of the energy; COLMAP's worst camera stays 1.9–2.2% of the scene off the truth against 3.9–10.9%. Estimates missed by −9% and +17% in time. docs.title: Resume here (handover, 2026-11-25)
docs.text:
A fresh session starts from this page. Updated after the RC-P8 GPU window (2026-11-25, 15:15 to 17:14): no Recce process runs on the X3 or the DGX, the homelab session has switched the DGX back to gpu-mode prod, and main holds everything finished. RC-P8's results and the 30,000-step courtyard splat are in their READMEs.

Tracker. The owner follows progress on a private page, Recce Step 0 Tracker, which mirrors this page. Republish it (read it first, then publish to the same link) whenever a row here changes.

Next, in order

  1. RC-P10: not proven (2026-11-26). Three Faro visits: 183 of 190 mesh distances within the limit; the seven failures (42444858, 1.0–1.1 m pairs, 2.2–3.8 cm short) are traced to one wall of a 1.05 m passage, about 1 cm from ARKit's poses there and the rest from the LiDAR surface; no room-wide bias, and three fusion settings leave it in place. Pose refinement (ICP or a pose graph) is the untried fix.
  2. RC-P6: proven (2026-11-26). M4 Pro 58.8 to 60.0 fps at a 60 Hz display's ceiling, met by the owner's judgement; the iPhone 15 Pro 50.0 against 30. Done (bb21a28): a cleaner splat (crop to the capture area, reduce by contribution in the training views).
  3. RC-P13: the drone and cave segments. The drone reconstruction is done (RC-P8, "Drone with RTK priors", 2026-11-26): RTK priors on half the photos fix scale (+0.025%) and the held-out half lands 0.31 m median from RTK with the OPENCV lens; a 0.2 m dome remains. The terrain model is built and checked (2026-11-26): the offset is split (RC-P8, "The height offset against the survey"), 0.25–0.38 m unexplained; the tolerance defaults to 2σ (configurable); the buildings segment is built on UseGeo Dataset-1 (2026-11-26): against OpenStreetMap it misses the fixed tolerance on outlines (63% of buildings pass, 80% needed); the mapper's bend is traced to the lens (2026-11-26); open are splitting houses of one roof height and the focal-height trade in nadir blocks with position priors (drone and buildings both read about 1.1 m low). The cave segment is built (2026-11-26); on the owner's tolerance (2% or 5 cm, 2026-11-27) it is not met. RC-P13 is closed as partly proven (2026-11-27).
  4. RC-P11 after RC-P8 or RC-P10 shows pose priors help. RC-P10's result (with poses and depth the rooms meet the wall limit; photos only, four of five split) is a finding; the owner puts it in context later (2026-11-25).

Decided by the owner (2026-11-27)

  • The cave tolerance is 2% or 5 cm; on it the cave segment is not met (11 of 17).
  • RC-P10 stays not proven with its cause recorded; pose refinement moves to the build phase.
  • RC-P13 closes as partly proven, each segment's verdict recorded.
  • Step 0 ends when the mock-ups (M2, M3, M4, M6, M7) have the owner's verdicts and a close-out report is written for RC-01 Vision. The report is written: Step 0 close-out report (2026-11-27).
  • AI is optional; Recce is complete without it. Every feature works from geometry and rules alone and is good enough on its own. AI is opt-in: Recce is an MCP server for a person's own agent, and a person can bring their own AI (an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, hosted or local) to take features further. Recorded in the brief; the mock-ups show both states.
  • The first case: the owner's home, captured with the iPhone app (owner, 2026-11-27). The build starts with the iPhone capture app (RC-P11) and the owner photographing at home, from simpler to more complex: objects first, then a whole room. The room is the setting the robots map, so it leads into the robot use cases. Recorded in the brief.
  • Learn mode is a feature inside the product (owner, 2026-11-27): the mini-labs and their tutor (RC-M5) live in Recce beside what they explain, not as a separate face.
  • Distribution is at the front, for work in the field (owner, 2026-11-27). The owner travels with a laptop and shoots with a camera, a drone or an underwater camera, and processes the day's work after. The answer is not a stronger laptop but offloading: the laptop sends work to the owner's other machines and to rented GPUs. Running workloads on other machines, rented GPUs included, is built from the beginning and is a key part of the vision, not a later scaling step. Open problems this raises: the upload (1,500 photos at 50 MB are 75 GB), whether the RAW files need to leave the laptop at all, and how work splits between the laptop and the remote workers before anything is sent. Recorded in the brief.
  • Both: Recce Studio on the desktop, and the web (owner, 2026-11-27): the web application packaged with the local engine in Electron, for macOS and Windows; RAW processing stays local.

Deferred by the owner (2026-11-26)

  • RC-P7 to the build phase: important, but not piloted in Step 0 (spec ready).
  • RC-P12's ranges clause to the underwater benchmark's site scene S1. RC-P12 is otherwise proven. Data on the X3: SQUID Satil (MD5 matches Zenodo's) and its evaluation code, AquaMVS core and data.zip (MD5 matches). SQUID is non-commercial: develop only, never redistribute.
  • The underwater benchmark capture (S1–S4, licence, the friend's set): decided after everything else in Step 0 is finished. The drone and Android dataset search is done: report (2026-11-26); fetching any of it is the owner's call.

Standing rules that carry over

  • Approved downloads and installs (user-level only): ETH3D and Mip-NeRF 360 data, MapAnything (Apache weights only), PyTorch, gsplat, texrecon, micromamba, Open3D, ARKitScenes subset, AquaMVS, SQUID, Blender, rawpy, the MCP SDK (RC-P3); three.js and Spark from a CDN and rerun-sdk (RC-P6's environment); scipy, tifffile and opencv-python-headless (RC-P12's environment). In throwaway Docker containers only (nothing on the host): CloudCompare, RTKLIB and laspy (2026-11-26). Datasets added 2026-11-26: the Etna lava tube (CC BY 4.0), two more ARKitScenes Faro visits, EuroSDR RPAS Phase 2/3 (CC BY 4.0) and UseGeo Dataset-1 (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; fetched with certificate checks off by the owner's decision, the host's certificate having expired in 2024). Anything else is asked first.
  • Recipes and profiles stay private (owner, 2026-11-26). What evaluation teaches (per-device corrections such as a focal-length fix, calibrated uncertainty models, tuned settings per capture scenario, the evaluation corpus and its scores) will live as data files in a separate private repository, next to the owner's data; the public engine loads them from a path and falls back to public defaults. Not built yet; new work keeps engine code generic and tuned values separable, so they can move there.
  • DGX GPU windows: standing go by day. Message the homelab session before switching; switch with ssh markodragoljevic@dgx-llm-1 '~/bin/gpu-mode-swap.sh free --json'; when the work's processes have exited, send it "done"; it switches back to prod and verifies both vLLMs. The claude account (reached through the Mac mini) runs the jobs and cannot switch modes.
  • The X3 is shared with eval-harness, which announces its test runs; heavy Recce work stays sequential and off cores it pins. The HIP build is the Docker image recce-p2-colmap-hip:latest.
  • Gate: make check; echo EXIT=$? before every commit, never a filtered line; commits land on main and CI is watched to a verdict.
  • Two parallel streams at most, on sonnet subagents; each writes only its own prototype folder and never commits.

docs.title: Open underwater benchmark: specification (2026-11-25)
docs.text:
RC-P12's last clause: specify the open underwater benchmark from what the public sets lack. This page lists the gaps, each with the evidence that shows it, then the benchmark that closes them. Numbers come from RC-P12 and public datasets, section "Underwater".

Recce starts from one case (see the brief, "Where this comes from"): 1,500 Nikon D850 photos of an underwater site that would not assemble on a laptop in a day. A benchmark that tests Recce underwater tests that case: a dive-scale set of high-resolution RAW photos from a camera in a housing, with ground truth for scale, shape and colour.

docs.title: What the public sets offer
docs.text: Set Views Geometric ground truth Colour reference RAW Port Licence AquaMVS Example 2 13-camera rig, 10 frames, lab ChArUco board, 60 mm squares None No Flat water surface, cameras in air CC BY 4.0 SQUID (4 sites) 57 stereo pairs Stereo range maps DGK charts at several distances Yes (NEF) Not documented CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 Sea-thru (D1–D5) About 1,100 images Range maps from Metashape Colour charts claimed, not checked No (linear PNG at 0.3x) Not checked CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 SeaThru-NeRF (4 scenes) Not stated COLMAP poses only None (images white-balanced) No Not checked Data licence not stated Submerged3D 4 scenes x 20 images, 720p None None No Not checked CC BY 4.0

docs.title: What they lack
docs.text:
1. Dive-scale multi-view sets with geometric ground truth. AquaMVS has a board in a tank; SQUID has stereo pairs; Sea-thru's ranges come from Metashape, a reconstruction rather than a measurement. No set found has hundreds of overlapping views of a site with independent scale and shape truth. RC-P12 shows why this matters: on SQUID Satil the eight stereo pairs barely overlap, only two small models register, and our dense depth keeps 0–1.1% of pixels.
  2. Colour references across many views. SQUID's charts sit in stereo pairs, so a correction can be scored but not built from a reconstruction of the same site; SeaThru-NeRF's images are already white-balanced. RC-P12 could not test range-based correction with ranges from our own reconstruction for this reason.
  3. Linear RAW with intact colour. Sea-thru ships linear PNGs at 0.3x, without RAW. SQUID ships RAW, but its TIFs clip red to zero on 78–99.9% of pixels, so anyone who uses the TIFs measures 37.9–40.8° from grey on every chart whatever their method does.
  4. Documented ports. AquaMVS models a flat water surface with the cameras in air. SQUID does not document its housing; our registration refines the focal length to 1.37–1.51 times the in-air value, which points at a flat port but is not confirmed. No set documents a dome port and where the lens's entrance pupil sits in it, which decides whether a pinhole model holds. On AquaMVS a pinhole calibration is off by −0.03% to −4.8% in scale depending on where the board is, against at most ±0.28% for the refractive model.
  5. Readable calibration. SQUID's calibration is a MATLAB stereoParameters object; its chart annotations sit a few pixels off its published undistorted images, because its evaluation undistorts on the fly. AquaMVS's corner pixels live on images undistorted with OpenCV's new camera matrix, not the calibration's K, which RC-P12 found only by reading their source.
  6. Size. The largest set with range maps (Sea-thru, about 1,100 images) is at 0.3x resolution and its ranges come from a reconstruction. Recce's founding case is 1,500 full-resolution RAW photos; distribution (RC-P7) and memory limits only show at that size.
  7. A permissive licence with truth. Of the sets with ground truth, only AquaMVS is CC BY; every set with colour references forbids commercial use.

docs.title: Scenes
docs.text: Scene What Why S1 Site One wreck or reef site, 1,000–2,000 RAW photos with a DSLR in a housing behind a dome port, in overlapping passes at two or three distances Gaps 1, 2, 6: Recce's founding case S2 Flat port A 100–200 photo subset of S1's area through a flat port Gap 4: the same site under both port models S3 Action camera A GoPro pass over S1's area The owner's second underwater camera; registration of mixed sets S4 Calibration A ChArUco board photographed through each port in the water, at three or more distances Gaps 4, 5: in-water calibration with its own truth, as AquaMVS does in a tank S5 Dive set The friend's dive set with its Metashape result, if the friend agrees to publish it A real-world baseline against the commercial tool

docs.title: Ground truth placed at the site
docs.text:
• Scale bars: two or more rigid bars with coded targets at a measured distance (tape or caliper, measured on land), seen from many views. Scored as scale error, as in RC-P9 and RC-P12.
  • Target network: six or more coded targets whose pairwise distances are taped underwater, giving a shape check independent of any reconstruction.
  • Colour charts: three or more identical charts at 1, 3 and 6 m from the main pass's camera path. Their patch values are measured above water under a known illuminant. This gives SQUID's test (charts at several ranges) in many overlapping views (gap 2).
  • Port record: port type and dimensions, and the lens's entrance pupil position relative to the dome centre, measured on land.

docs.title: Measures
docs.text:
Every measure already exists in a prototype, so the benchmark adds no new scoring code.

Measure From Registration rate, time and cost RC-P1, RC-P7 Scale error on the scale bars; target-distance error; rigid RMSE RC-P9, RC-P12 (AquaMVS) Dense and mesh accuracy against the target network RC-P4 Grey-ramp angle to grey, ramp contrast against range, chart-pair angle RC-P12 (SQUID) Splat quality on held-out views RC-P4

docs.title: Format
docs.text:
• RAW files as they come from the camera, EXIF untouched; no derived TIFs in the release.
  • Calibration as plain JSON in OpenCV's convention (K, distortion, R, t, port parameters), readable without MATLAB.
  • Target and chart annotations in the pixel grid of the RAW files, with the code that produced them, so no annotation depends on an undistortion step the user cannot repeat.
  • Measured distances and chart patch values as CSV, with the instrument and its stated accuracy.
  • Licence CC BY 4.0 for the owner's own captures; S5 under whatever the friend agrees to.

docs.title: Open, for the owner
docs.text:
• Whether to capture S1–S4, and when: one or two dives, plus a pool session for S4.
  • The licence for the owner's captures; CC BY 4.0 is the proposal.
  • Whether the friend's dive set (S5) can be published, or stays a private baseline.
  • RC-P12's "ranges from the reconstruction" clause moved to S1 (owner, 2026-11-26); S1 is where it is tested.

docs.title: Verification of open facts (2026-11-24)
docs.text: This note checks the facts marked "to verify" or "unknown" in docs/concept/RC-brief.md, docs/concept/RC-use-cases.md and docs/reference/*.md against primary sources: Apple Developer and Support pages, GoPro's manual and product pages, GitHub and GitLab repositories, dataset pages, the papers and the conda-forge and PyPI indexes. [V] means the page was read on 2026-11-24; [U] means it was not (search snippet or memory). Apple's iPhone User Guide pages read today carry the current (iOS 26) text; the iPhone 15 Pro statements rest on the iOS 17-era Apple article 119916 where it matters. Several items need a test on the real device; they are listed at the end. The search/fetch budget of about 30 was exceeded (about 50 calls) because several vendor pages are JavaScript shells and needed a second route.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: Item Answer V/U Consequence 1a iPhone default resolution Camera app default is 24 MP HEIF (changeable to 12 MP). 48 MP only via Resolution Control: HEIF Max, JPEG Max or RAW Max; ProRAW is 12 or 48 MP. Ultra Wide, Telephoto, Night, flash and macro: 12 MP only V Capture protocol must say "HEIF Max or RAW Max, 1x main camera"; default shots are 24 MP 1b Safari HEIC upload Safari transcodes a file whose type is not in the accept list, to the first type listed; image/* was treated as a literal string until a fix in Jan 2026. "Most Compatible" changes the capture format to JPEG V Set accept explicitly and test on the phone; do not assume HEIC arrives or is converted 1c Macro auto-switch Yes, can be turned off: in-camera Auto Macro button, and Settings > Camera > Macro Control V Protocol: turn Auto Macro off, shoot at 1x; ultra-wide macro is 12 MP anyway 1d ProRAW processing ProRAW is captured together with Smart HDR, Deep Fusion or Night mode, so it is not unprocessed sensor data V Do not treat ProRAW as radiometrically linear; per-photo tone mapping can still differ 1e ARKit captureHighResolutionFrame exists, iOS 16+, needs a high-res video format. World frame y-up, right-handed, camera starts looking down -z. sceneDepth needs LiDAR (iOS 14+). Resolution on iPhone 15 Pro, default capturedImage size, intrinsics drift and 256x192 depth are not on Apple's doc pages V (API, axes), U (sizes), unsettled (15 Pro size, intrinsics drift) Log intrinsics and image size per frame on the device before relying on a fixed K 2a HERO13 RAW .gpr (DNG-based) in Photo, Burst, Night, Time Lapse photo and Night Lapse photo, only with SuperPhoto off, digital lens Wide, zoom off, Time Lapse interval 5 s or more, Night Lapse shutter 5 s or more V (manual copy hosted by Adorama) P-GoPro runs use Wide + RAW; lens is Wide, which is the most distorted mode 2b HERO13 lens modes Photo: Wide (16-34 mm) and Linear (19-39 mm) only. Time-lapse video: TimeWarp has HyperView, SuperView, Wide, Linear, Linear + Horizon Lock; Time Lapse and Night Lapse video have Wide and Linear; Star Trails, Light Painting, Vehicle Light Trails have Wide. Video also has Narrow (high-fps presets). No Max SuperView V No Narrow, HyperView or SuperView in stills; RAW forces Wide; Linear is the lowest-distortion still mode 2c HB lens mods Macro: manual focus ring 11-75 cm. Ultra Wide: up to 177 degrees FOV. Anamorphic: 21:9 with in-camera de-squeeze. ND 4-pack: ND4, 8, 16, 32. Camera auto-detects the mod V A mod is a different optical system: calibrate it as its own camera; Macro mod is the only close-focus route 2d Lens mode in metadata GPMF defines VFOV (L/S/W/H), ZFOV, PRJT, DZOM/DZMX; GPMF README says header metadata is in all MP4 and JPG files; ExifTool reads GPMF from the JPEG APP6 segment. Whether a HERO13 photo writes VFOV is not confirmed V (spec), unsettled (actual files) Run exiftool -G1 -a -u on a real HERO13 JPG and GPR before the ingest stage depends on it 2e Stock minimum focus Not published on the pages read (manual, product pages). Only a marketing claim that the Macro mod focuses "4X closer" V (absence), unsettled Measure on the camera with a ruler target 3a Mip-NeRF 360 licence No licence or terms on the project page; the code repo (multinerf) is Apache-2.0; the zip's contents were not inspected V (page), unsettled Local development only; ask the authors or inspect the zip before any release 3b COLMAP datasets South Building 128 images at 3072x2304 (checked in the zip); Gerrard Hall 100, Person Hall 330, Graham Hall 1273 images; resolution of the last three not checked; no licence stated; download from github.com/colmap/colmap releases 3.11.1 V Graham Hall stays the only 1,000+ set but is a roughly 11.8 GB multipart download; resolution still to check 3c ETH3D evaluation Tolerances 1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50 cm; tool is ETH3D/multi-view-evaluation, BSD licence, depends on Boost, Eigen, PCL V Evaluation can run locally and be bundled; GitHub shows "NOASSERTION" only because the file is LICENSE.txt 3d SQUID targets Identical waterproof colour charts from DGK Color Tools at several distances, plus a calibration checkerboard; RAW, TIF, calibration files and distance maps; 57 stereo pairs, 4 sites V Usable for colour-chart checks (P8); exact DGK chart model not stated 3e AquaMVS licence MIT (LICENSE file and PyPI metadata) V No licence blocker 4 Refractive COLMAP New BSD (COPYING.txt, underwater branch). Not merged upstream: no refractive model in COLMAP main. No pycolmap bindings found in the fork V (licence, models.h), "not found" (bindings) Treat as a separate C++ build; refractive SfM is CLI only, no Python path 5 Akkaynak and Treibitz 2018 paper: backscatter coefficients differ from direct-transmission coefficients. Range and reflectance dependence of the attenuation coefficient was shown earlier and is restated in the 2019 paper. docs.title: 1a. Default photo resolution
docs.text:
• "On supported models, you can change the default resolution of the Main or Fusion cameras from 24 MP to 12 MP... To capture resolution at 48 MP, go to Settings > Camera > Formats, then turn on Resolution Control or ProRAW & Resolution Control." [V https://support.apple.com/guide/iphone/change-advanced-camera-settings-iphb362b394e/ios]
  • iPhone 14 Pro and later with iOS 17: formats HEIF Max and RAW Max give up to 48 MP; RAW 12 gives 12 MP; standard HEIF gives up to 24 MP. ProRAW files are about 25 MB at 12 MP and about 75 MB at 48 MP. "Only photos that you take with the main camera at 1x can be saved 48 MP. Ultra Wide, Telephoto, Night mode, flash, and macro photos can only be saved at 12 MP." [V https://support.apple.com/en-us/119916]
  • The 24 MP default is a Camera-app mode. AVFoundation on iPhone 15 Pro lists only 12 MP and 48 MP in supportedMaxPhotoDimensions (Apple forum answer, Nov 2023) [V https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/738418, a user post, not Apple documentation; may be outdated].

docs.title: 1b. Safari upload and HEIC
docs.text:
• WebKit bug 303803: Safari 17+ transcodes an uploaded file to the first MIME type in the accept list when the file's own type is not in the list. Because image/* was matched as a literal string, accept="image/*,image/heic" turned PNG and JPEG into HEIC. The wildcard fix was committed in January 2026. [V https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=303803; page read through the fetch tool's summary]
  • Apple developer forum report of the same behaviour (a .jpeg arrives as tempImage....heic). [V https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/743049]
  • "Most Compatible" (JPEG) versus "High Efficiency" (HEIF) is the capture format under Settings > Camera > Formats; it applies when RAW is off. [V https://support.apple.com/en-us/119916]
  • Not settled: what the photo picker hands Safari for a HEIC original with a plain accept="image/jpeg", and whether a ProRAW DNG passes through unchanged. Needs a test page on the phone with each accept variant and a log of File.type, name and size.

docs.title: 1c. Macro control
docs.text:
• "Get close to the subject, as close as 2 centimeters. Camera will automatically switch to the Ultra Wide camera." An on-screen button turns automatic macro switching off. "To turn off the manual Macro Control... go to Settings > Camera, then turn off Macro Control"; Settings > Camera > Preserve Settings keeps the choice between sessions. [V https://support.apple.com/guide/iphone/take-macro-photos-and-videos-iphfaacf2eb0/ios]
  • The page does not say which setting state is the default on an iPhone 15 Pro. Check on the phone.

docs.title: 1d. ProRAW and computational processing
docs.text:
• "Apple ProRAW combines the information of a standard RAW format along with iPhone image processing"; capture works "including when also using the Smart HDR, Deep Fusion, or Night mode features." [V https://support.apple.com/en-us/119916]
  • ProRAW is not available with Live Photos, Portrait mode or video. [V same page]

docs.title: 1e. ARKit
docs.text:
• ARSession.captureHighResolutionFrame(completion:): iOS 16.0+, iPadOS 16.0+. Delivers a frame out-of-band with pose, anchors and semantics filled in; fails if a previous request is pending. For the highest resolution choose a non-binned ARConfiguration.VideoFormat, e.g. recommendedVideoFormatForHighResolutionFrameCapturing. [V https://developer.apple.com/documentation/arkit/arsession/capturehighresolutionframe(completion:), read via Apple's documentation JSON feed]
  • Resolution: the WWDC22 session says "on my iPhone 13 that means the full 12 megapixels of the wide camera"; 4K video mode is 3840x2160 at 30 fps (iPhone 11 and later). [V https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/wwdc2022/10126/] The iPhone 15 Pro value is not stated by Apple: unsettled. A DTS reply on an iPhone 16 Pro thread says 48 MP ultra-wide capture during an AR session has "no supported way". [V https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/769604]
  • ARFrame.capturedImage: full-range planar YCbCr (BT.601) pixel buffer. The doc page gives no size. 1920x1440 is the commonly quoted default [U, forum snippet].
  • ARCamera.intrinsics: 3x3 matrix in pixels (fx, fy, px, py, origin at the centre of the upper-left pixel), "based on physical characteristics of the device camera and a pinhole camera model." [V https://developer.apple.com/documentation/arkit/arcamera/intrinsics] The page does not say whether it changes per frame: unsettled.
  • World frame: with .gravity alignment "the y-axis is parallel to gravity", z-axis basis (0,0,-1) points where the device camera faces at session start, x-axis by the right-hand rule; "World coordinate space in ARKit always follows a right-handed convention." [V https://developer.apple.com/documentation/arkit/arconfiguration/worldalignment-swift.enum/gravity; https://developer.apple.com/documentation/arkit/arcamera/transform] Camera space: z points away from the screen side, so the camera looks along its own -z (consistent with the doc's wording, not stated in one sentence).
  • sceneDepth: needs LiDAR, iOS 14.0+, nil unless the frame semantic is enabled; depthMap is metres. [V https://developer.apple.com/documentation/arkit/arconfiguration/framesemantics-swift.struct/scenedepth; https://developer.apple.com/documentation/arkit/ardepthdata/depthmap] 256x192 is stated by forum answers and the search snippet, not by an Apple doc page I read [U].

docs.title: 2. GoPro HERO13 Black
docs.text: Source for 2a, 2b: the HERO13 Black user manual, a copy hosted at https://www.adorama.com/col/productManuals/GPHERO13A.pdf (GoPro's own document, retailer host; gopro.com help pages are JavaScript shells and did not render) [V].

docs.title: 2a. RAW
docs.text: "All photos are saved as a .jpg image... and a .gpr file", DNG-based. Available for Photo, Burst, Night, Time Lapse photo and Night Lapse photo with: SuperPhoto off, digital lens Wide, zoom off, not for continuous photos, Time Lapse interval at least 5 s, Night Lapse shutter at least 5 s. HDR also does not work with RAW. Photo resolution 27 MP at 8:7.

docs.title: 2b. Lens modes
docs.text:
• Photo: manual says "3 lens options" but its table lists Wide (16-34 mm) and Linear (19-39 mm). The third is not shown; treat the photo list as Wide and Linear until a device check.
  • Video: HyperView (16 mm), SuperView (16 mm), Wide (16-34 mm), Linear + Horizon Lock/Leveling (19-33 mm), Linear (19-39 mm); Narrow appears in high-frame-rate presets. No "Max SuperView" on this camera.
  • Time lapse table: TimeWarp (5.3K, 4K, 1080p): HyperView, SuperView, Wide, Linear, Linear + Horizon Lock. Star Trails, Light Painting, Vehicle Light Trails: Wide. Time Lapse Video and Night Lapse Video: Wide, Linear.
  • GoPro's product page spec list: 27 MP photos [V https://gopro.com/en/us/shop/cameras/learn/hero13black/CHDHX-131-master.html].

docs.title: 2c. HB-series lens mods (HERO13 Black only)
docs.text:
• Macro Lens Mod: rotating focus ring, 4.33 in (11 cm) to 2.46 ft (75 cm), focus peaking, "4x closer" than the stock lens. [V https://gopro.com/en/us/shop/mounts-accessories/macro-lens-mod/AEWAL-021.html]
  • Ultra Wide Lens Mod: FOV up to 177 degrees (36% wider, 48% taller), 1:1 aspect, Horizon Lock on all lenses, vertical capture. [V https://gopro.com/en/us/shop/mounts-accessories/ultra-wide-lens-mod/AEWAL-001.html]
  • Anamorphic Lens Mod: 21:9 ultra-wide cinematic look, horizontal flares, in-camera de-squeeze. [V https://gopro.com/en/us/shop/mounts-accessories/anamorphic-lens-mod/AEWAL-011.html]
  • ND Filter 4-Pack: ND4, ND8, ND16, ND32; camera detects the filter and enters Auto Cinematic video mode. [V https://gopro.com/en/us/shop/mounts-accessories/smart-motion-blur-nd-filter/AENDF-001.html]
  • All mods are auto-detected. The manual's settings list includes "Lens Mod Mode". Which of the mods apply to stills (as opposed to video presets) is not stated in the pages read: unsettled, test.

docs.title: 2d. Lens mode in metadata
docs.text:
• GPMF spec: "there is a lot of metadata in the header for all MP4 and JPG files"; VFOV = "L - Linear, W - wide, S - Superview, H - Hyperview"; ZFOV = diagonal FOV in degrees; PRJT = lens projection; DZOM/DZMX = digital zoom. [V https://github.com/gopro/gpmf-parser/blob/main/README.md]
  • ExifTool: GPMF tags are extracted from "the APP6 'GoPro' segment of JPEG files"; table includes VFOV, ZFOV, LensProjection. [V https://exiftool.org/TagNames/GoPro.html]
  • Not confirmed: that a HERO13 still (JPG or GPR) carries VFOV and ZFOV. Unsettled.

docs.title: 2e. Stock minimum focus
docs.text: Not given in the manual text searched (no focus-distance entry) nor on the product pages. Unsettled; measure.

docs.title: 3a. Mip-NeRF 360
docs.text: The project page lists 360_v2.zip (12.5 GB) and 360_extra_scenes.zip and states no licence or terms. [V https://jonbarron.info/mipnerf360/] The code repository google-research/multinerf is Apache-2.0 [V GitHub API]. The zip's contents (any LICENSE or README inside) were not inspected: a partial download was started and cancelled. Unsettled.

docs.title: 3b. COLMAP datasets
docs.text:
• Counts from the COLMAP docs: Gerrard Hall 100, Graham Hall 1273, Person Hall 330, South Building 128 (UNC Chapel Hill; "same camera", wide-angle lens). [V https://github.com/colmap/colmap/blob/main/doc/datasets.rst; https://demuc.de/colmap/datasets/]
  • South Building: downloaded and counted, 128 images, 3072x2304, Panasonic DMC-TZ3 (EXIF). [V]
  • Licence: none stated on either page. Resolution of Gerrard, Person and Graham not checked (an attempt to read the first JPEG from the multipart zips returned nothing).
  • Downloads (all https://github.com/colmap/colmap/releases/download/3.11.1/): south-building.zip (419 MB), gerrard-hall.zip (1.0 GB), person-hall.z01 + person-hall.zip, graham-hall.z01-z05 + graham-hall.zip (zip 1.29 GB; z01 2.10 GB; if each part is that size, about 11.8 GB in total, only z01 measured). The page tells to recombine multipart archives with zip -FF. [V]

docs.title: 3c. ETH3D
docs.text:
• README of the tool: ETH3DMultiViewEvaluation --reconstruction_ply_path ... --ground_truth_mlp_path ... --tolerances 0.01,0.02,0.05,0.1,0.2,0.5 (metres), i.e. 1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50 cm. [V https://github.com/ETH3D/multi-view-evaluation] The CVPR 2017 paper evaluates "distance thresholds from 1cm to 50cm" and reports category tables at 2 cm [V https://www.eth3d.net/data/schoeps2017cvpr.pdf]. The benchmark page shows F1 at 1 and 2 cm and accuracy and completeness at 1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50 cm [V https://www.eth3d.net/high_res_multi_view].
  • Licence: LICENSE.txt reads "This program is released under the BSD license", copyright 2017 Thomas Schoeps, Johannes L. Schoenberger. [V raw file] Dependencies: Boost.Filesystem, Eigen, PCL [V https://www.eth3d.net/documentation]. Last push 2023-04-11.

docs.title: 3d. SQUID
docs.text: Berman, Levy, Avidan, Treibitz: 57 stereo pairs from four sites (Katzaa 15, Satil 8, Nachsholim 13, Mikhmoret 21). The page lists RAW images, TIF files, camera calibration files and distance maps. [V https://csms.haifa.ac.il/profiles/tTreibitz/datasets/ambient_forwardlooking/index.html] The TPAMI paper: "identical waterproof color charts (from DGK Color Tools)" at different distances, a calibration checkerboard on the rig, Nikon D810 with 35 mm lens in a dome port, natural light only. [V https://arxiv.org/abs/1811.01343, full text read] Licence: the page asks for citation; no licence text. Chart model and patch count: unsettled.

docs.title: 3e. AquaMVS
docs.text: McGrathLab/AquaMVS: MIT, copyright 2026 tlancaster6. [V https://github.com/McGrathLab/AquaMVS; PyPI metadata license_expression: MIT]

docs.title: 4. Refractive COLMAP
docs.text:
• Fork of COLMAP on GitLab (branch underwater), mirrored at https://github.com/MDSKiel/colmap_underwater (default branch underwater, last push 2024-10-29). Licence: COPYING.txt is COLMAP's new BSD text ("Copyright (c) 2023, ETH Zurich and UNC Chapel Hill") [V https://cau-git.rz.uni-kiel.de/inf-ag-koeser/colmap_underwater/-/raw/underwater/COPYING.txt]. GitHub reports NOASSERTION because of the file name.
  • README: features are flat-port and dome-port refractive camera models, refractive SfM, bundle adjustment with pose priors; "Building COLMAP Underwater from source is exactly the same as building the original COLMAP"; cite She, Seegraeber, Nakath, Koeser, "Refractive COLMAP: Refractive Structure-from-Motion Revisited", IROS 2024. Mentions a calibration toolbox calibmar. [V https://cau-git.rz.uni-kiel.de/inf-ag-koeser/colmap_underwater/-/raw/underwater/README.md]
  • Upstream: src/colmap/sensor/models.h on COLMAP main has no refractive or flat-port model, and the camera-model doc page has no match for "refract" or "flat port". [V raw files today] I did not check upstream pull requests (GitHub code search needs authentication).
  • pycolmap: the mirror's top-level tree has no python or pycolmap directory and the README does not mention pycolmap. I did not find bindings. arXiv 2403.08640 not re-read today.

docs.title: 5. Akkaynak and Treibitz
docs.text:
• "A Revised Underwater Image Formation Model", Derya Akkaynak and Tali Treibitz, CVPR 2018, pp. 6723-6732. Abstract: "the wideband coefficients that govern backscatter are different than those that govern direct transmission". [V https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content_cvpr_2018/html/Akkaynak_A_Revised_Underwater_CVPR_2018_paper.html]
  • "Sea-Thru: A Method for Removing Water From Underwater Images", CVPR 2019, pp. 1682-1691. Abstract states both findings: the signal attenuation coefficient "depends on object range and reflectance", and the backscatter coefficient "differs from the signal attenuation coefficient"; the method uses RGBD images. [V https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content_CVPR_2019/html/Akkaynak_Sea-Thru_A_Method_for_Removing_Water_From_Underwater_Images_CVPR_2019_paper.html]
  • Correction to the working claim: the 2018 abstract attributes the earlier range-dependence finding to prior work ("we recently showed"); the 2018 paper's own new result is the backscatter finding. The earlier work is likely the CVPR 2017 attenuation-coefficient paper [U, not read].

docs.title: 6. COLMAP dense
docs.text:
• Current release: COLMAP 4.2.1 (09/29/2026). [V https://github.com/colmap/colmap/blob/main/CHANGELOG.rst; GitHub releases API]
  • FAQ: "If you do not have a CUDA-enabled GPU but some other GPU, you can use all COLMAP functionality except the dense reconstruction part." [V https://github.com/colmap/colmap/blob/main/doc/faq.rst]
  • Install doc: CUDA build, or HIP/ROCm build (-DCUDA_ENABLED=OFF -DHIP_ENABLED=ON); "The HIP backend accelerates dense reconstruction (patch_match_stereo) and GPU SIFT". Changelog: "Added ROCm/HIP acceleration for patch_match_stereo... CUDA and HIP builds are mutually exclusive." [V https://github.com/colmap/colmap/blob/main/doc/install.rst; CHANGELOG.rst]
  • No CPU or Metal path for patch_match_stereo in install, FAQ, tutorial, CLI docs or changelog (grep for "metal" returns nothing). colmap.github.io/dense.html is a script shell and did not render; the repository doc/*.rst sources were read instead.

docs.title: 7. pycolmap
docs.text:
• Current: 4.2.1 on PyPI, Python 3.10+. Wheels: manylinux_2_28_x86_64, macosx_14_0_arm64, win_amd64 for cp310-cp314. pycolmap-cuda12 4.2.1: manylinux_2_28_x86_64 only. [V https://pypi.org/project/pycolmap/, PyPI JSON]
  • Docs: wheels via pip; CUDA wheels only for Linux x86_64 ("for now"); source build = install COLMAP from source, then python -m pip install . on Linux and macOS. [V https://github.com/colmap/colmap/blob/main/doc/pycolmap/index.rst] The docs do not mention aarch64 or CUDA on aarch64 specifically; the generic COLMAP CUDA build applies. Unsettled for an aarch64 source build until tried.
  • conda-forge pycolmap 4.2.1: linux-aarch64 has cpu, cuda_129 and cuda_134 builds (GPL and LGPL variants); osx-64 has CPU builds only; osx-arm64, linux-64, win-64 also present. [V https://anaconda.org/conda-forge/pycolmap, anaconda API listing]

docs.title: Still unsettled
docs.text:
1. Safari upload of HEIC and ProRAW DNG from the photo picker for each accept variant: test page on the iPhone 15 Pro.
  2. iPhone 15 Pro captureHighResolutionFrame pixel size (expected 12 MP, not documented), default capturedImage size, and whether ARCamera.intrinsics varies frame to frame: log on the device.
  3. Whether Macro Control is on by default in Settings on the owner's phone.
  4. HERO13 stills: third photo digital lens in the manual's "3 options"; whether VFOV, ZFOV and PRJT are written into HERO13 JPG and GPR; whether lens mods work for stills; stock minimum focus distance: shoot and run exiftool -G1 -a -u -ee.
  5. Mip-NeRF 360 data licence: inspect the zip contents or ask the authors.
  6. Resolution and licence of Gerrard Hall, Person Hall, Graham Hall: unpack one image from each.
  7. SQUID chart model and licence terms.
  8. Refractive COLMAP: upstream PRs, and any Python bindings beyond the mirror's top-level tree; arXiv 2403.08640 not re-read.
  9. pycolmap source build with CUDA on Linux aarch64: documented only generically; conda-forge builds exist and are the lower-risk route. COLMAP HIP on gfx1151 untested.
  10. Akkaynak 2017 attenuation-coefficient paper (title and venue) was not read.

docs.title: Visual ideas and the mock-up plan
docs.text:
The catalogue of concepts for the 3D scene, the explanations and the frame, and the mock-ups that work them out. The direction behind them is in the brief §2 ("Two registers in one interface"); the mock-up track is in §5 ("Two tracks, one meeting point"). Every entry is a direction to mock, not a decision: a mock-up keeps, changes or drops it, with a reason.

Sources: ideas 1–8 were proposed on 2026-11-24 and approved by the owner the same day; ideas 9–20 and the patterns come from the UX inspiration research of the same day, also approved as directions. Source tags [V] and [U] there apply here.

docs.title: The ideas
docs.text: # Idea What it explains Source Mock-up 1 The model builds itself on screen. Each photo's camera snaps into place and the point cloud fills in as registration runs; afterwards it replays as a short film of the reconstruction. How registration works, and where it went wrong Owner session M1 2 Matches drawn as threads. Thin lines link each photo to the points it sees; a part held by few threads looks fragile. Why a part of the model is weak, before any error number Owner session M1 3 Gaps as light and shadow. Areas no photo covered are dim, well-covered areas lit; the next shot appears as a ghost camera that can be sent to a phone or a robot. Coverage, and what to capture next Owner session M2 4 Confidence on the surface. Uncertain geometry is drawn sketchy or translucent, solid geometry solid, instead of a rainbow error map; uncertainty blends softly between cameras rather than as a patchwork. Uncertainty, read at a glance Owner session; Womp soft blending M2 5 An agent narrates the run. A multimodal agent looks at the intermediate products and writes a short illustrated debrief ("the left side of the wreck rests on 12 photos; here are the three that hold it"). The whole run, in words and pictures Owner session M3 6 Compare like a photographer. A before/after split slider: COLMAP against GLOMAP, JPEG against RAW, one recipe against another, on the same view. What a strategy or recipe changed Owner session; Resolve wipe M4 7 A presentation mode. Lighting, framing and a camera path for showing a model to people outside the field; a first-class output, shareable as a browser link with no install. The result, to an audience Owner session; Shapr3D review link M6 8 Underwater, made visible. Toggle between the water's colour and the corrected colour; the refraction correction shown as a lens of water that can be switched off. Colour loss and refraction Owner session M7 9 Plural timelines. A run has a timeline per axis (photo order, capture time, registration order, optimiser iteration); a picker chooses which drives the scene; static facts (intrinsics, scale reference) belong to all of them. That a reconstruction has more than one "when" Rerun M1 10 Evidence handles. Every sentence and number in a debrief or report has a handle that selects its photos or matches and flies the camera there; a sentence without one is flagged as unsupported. Phrases open in place to show their photos. Why to believe a claim Agent UX pattern; Spline MCP; Nicky Case's Nutshell M3 11 The engine's belief at step k. Scrub what the engine believed at each iteration, including poses it later discarded. Hidden state: how the solver got there Bret Victor M1 12 Mini-labs. Small reader-driven demonstrations beside a term (baseline and triangulation, overlap and match count, blur and features, rolling shutter, refraction and focal length), one or two controls each. The concepts themselves, by touch Ciechanowski; Distill M5 13 A shared coverage glyph. One ring or sphere glyph that fills as angles are covered, drawn the same on the web, the phone and an operator's tablet, with named reasons for its advice. Coverage, learned once, read everywhere Apple's capture dial M2, M8 14 Honest colour. Every ramp in the scene is perceptually uniform (built in LCH), with a colour-blind-safe variant, a luminance-only fallback and a "what this colour means" legend on every overlay. That equal steps in the data look equal Linear M2 (rule for all) 15 One verb list. One registry of actions powers the command palette (Cmd+K), the CLI subcommands, the HTTP routes and the MCP tools. That people and agents do the same things Raycast; Rerun M0 16 Readiness stamps. The quality report ends with named uses (survey, robot localisation, print, web viewing), each pass, fail or unknown against stated requirements. What the model is good for NVIDIA Omniverse SimReady M3 17 Live registration during capture. For a streaming source each arriving frame registers into the model in view; a frame that fails shows as a ghost at its expected pose. That the capture is working, while it happens Capture One tethering; Apple point-cloud preview M8 18 The agent as a scene editor. The agent places ghost cameras, labels and a camera path into the scene through MCP; the person moves or deletes them. Agent and person working on one scene Spline MCP M3 19 Replay the moment. One click replays the iterations around the step with the largest residual jump, with camera positions before and after shown as a fading trail. Where it went wrong, without searching NASA Eyes replay; Flightradar24 trails M1 20 Frame the cost. Every recipe shows a time and energy estimate before it runs and the measured figure after. What a choice costs Autodesk Flow Studio credits M4 21 The gap list for the next session. After an upload, every gap is listed and ranked, not only the weakest: thin coverage, few photos, photos that did not join, pieces that did not connect, missing scale. Each gap becomes a shot card: where to stand (a ghost camera, and the nearest photo already taken as a reference to recognise the spot), what to shoot and why. A top-down map numbers the gaps; the next upload ticks closed gaps off. The same list goes to the phone app, and to a robot as a machine-readable brief. Not route planning. What to do tomorrow, in the field Owner, 2026-11-24 M2

docs.title: Patterns for every surface
docs.text:
• One time cursor drives every panel (Rerun, Foxglove): scene, photo strip, match graph and plots move together, with no visible lag.
  • Analysis is an overlay, never a replacement (Halide's zebras and peaking, Forma's layers): each overlay has one toggle and leaves the scene underneath.
  • Show the data, show hidden state, concrete before abstract (Bret Victor): explanations start from one camera and one point, then widen to the whole set.
  • Drill in with breadcrumbs (Blender 5.0): run, stage, step, without losing place.
  • Recipes are node graphs with swap-in-place (Houdini, Blender's Swap Node): a strategy is swapped and keeps its connections; two recipes compare by the node that differs.
  • Motion is optional (Blender's Reduce Motion): every animation has a still equivalent.
  • A camera is its photo (owner, 2026-11-24, restated 2026-11-27): a photo hangs where it was taken as a crisp image plane with no outline; a dot marks the camera centre; four hairline rays run from the photo's corners and fade towards the centre, so the light reads as travelling and the photo as the surface. No edges close a pyramid. A shot not yet taken is a dotted outline with faint rays. Every scene with cameras follows this. A setting replaces the photos with a solid fill (owner, 2026-11-27), for large sets or slow devices where hundreds of textures cost frame rate; the dot and the fading rays stay the same. Not built yet; its saving is not measured.
  • AI is a layer, never a dependency (owner, 2026-11-27): each view works with no AI connected; with the person's own AI connected, what it adds is marked as written by AI and checked against the engine's numbers.
  • The AI is a coach (owner, 2026-11-27): why the result is as it is, a plan made only of actions from the engine's menu (each "engine" or "next capture"), how the operator will know it worked, and what the facts cannot say. The rule writes a plan from the same facts without AI. Shared checker: mockups/coach_lib.py; first in RC-M7, then RC-M2, RC-M1 and, as a tutor, RC-M5.
  • The frame follows robotics-lab (Observatory, Mission Control): dark by default, outliner, read-only inspector, label left and value right in mono; tokens derived from base, accent and contrast (Linear's approach).

docs.title: The mock-ups
docs.text:
Each mock-up is a page in mockups/RC-M<n>-<slug>/, built to be looked at and critiqued. It uses real prototype output wherever it exists; where it does not, it says plainly which data is stand-in. A mock-up ends with the owner's verdict per concept: kept, changed or dropped, with the reason.

Mock-up Shows Ideas Data M0 — The frame The shell every view lives in: top bar, outliner, inspector, timeline, command palette, light and dark 15, patterns Any M1 — The run A reconstruction replayed: cameras snapping in, threads, plural timelines, belief at step k, replay the moment 1, 2, 9, 11, 19 RC-P1 kicker (COLMAP and GLOMAP) M2 — Coverage and confidence Light and shadow, ghost camera, the coverage glyph, confidence on the surface, honest colour 3, 4, 13, 14 RC-P1, then RC-P4 meshes M3 — The debrief The agent's illustrated report with evidence handles, readiness stamps, agent-placed annotations 5, 10, 16, 18 RC-P1 and RC-P3 quality state M4 — Recipes and comparison The recipe graph, swap-in-place, split-slider compare, cost before and after 6, 20 RC-P1's two strategies M5 — Learn Mini-labs beside the terms of the primer 12 Synthetic, by design M6 — Presentation Lighting, framing, camera path, shareable link 7 RC-P4 mesh and splat M7 — Underwater Water colour against corrected colour, the refraction lens 8 RC-P12 public underwater sets M8 — Capture The phone's coverage glyph and live registration 13, 17 RC-P11 iPhone app

Order: M0 and M1 first (they set the frame and use the data RC-P1 already has), then M2, M3 and M4; M5–M8 follow the prototypes they depend on.

docs.title: Decided by the owner (2026-11-24)
docs.text:
• Technology: mock-ups are plain HTML with three.js; the product's UI moves to its own stack later. Whether that stack is SvelteKit (the default in the owner's other projects) is reopened and decided on evidence from the mock-ups, not by habit.
  • Two passes: phase 1 is rough but still good-looking, to settle the concepts; phase 2 polishes the chosen direction.
